title: The need for electrolyte innovation in next-generation batteries
abstract: Over the past decade, battery electrolytes have evolved from a mere ion-conducting media into active regulators of the electrode reaction, interfacial chemistry and cycling stability. Innovations spanning advanced liquid, solid-state and emerging electrolyte systems are opening new pathways towards safer, higher-energy and application-specific batteries.

title: Resilience as a governing principle in water governance
abstract: Water governance often treats resilience as an end state, achieved mainly through technocratic decision-making and standard engineering tools. Drawing on five international cases, we argue that resilience should instead guide governance design and operation through adaptability, coordination, learning and accountability.

title: Accounting for the mining industry’s global water footprint
abstract: Millions of people share rivers, aquifers and coastlines with mining operations, but years of regulation and voluntary schemes have left these communities with limited knowledge of what water is withdrawn, discharged or contaminated. De-risking the sector requires mandatory transparency, which should be made a condition of the capital now flowing into critical mineral supply chains.

abstract: Attacks on critical water infrastructure have become normalized in modern military conflict. To counter this, argues Hussam Hussein, water scientists must build and maintain real-time monitoring and documentation infrastructure in active conflict zones.

title: Water as our common denominator in the fragmented world
abstract: In the era of growing political polarization, water can be a force for cooperation towards a global agenda of unity, security, prosperity and sustainability, argues Kaveh Madani.

title: Sinking land is the fingerprint of global water bankruptcy
abstract: Land subsidence is the physical fingerprint of irreversible groundwater loss, yet remains absent from water governance. Embedding it as an early warning metric could help societies act before depletion becomes water bankruptcy.

title: Confronting water bankruptcy
abstract: With 2030 and the conclusion of the current round of Sustainable Development Goals on the horizon, the world has entered a state of water bankruptcy. A collection of opinion and research explores how this bankruptcy affects environmental and social systems and asks how we return to sustainable and resilient water futures.

title: Photobiocatalysis at the interface of biocatalysis and biomimetic chemocatalysis
abstract: This Perspective analyses representative photobiocatalytic systems to uncover the synergies between biomimetic and chemomimetic strategies and provides a framework for future developments in the field.

title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
abstract: Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light-matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6-arising from collective quantum interference among emitters-has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open new opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8-10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
abstract: Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1-3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune-metabolic homeostasis4-9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1. Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope2,3. Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

title: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions
abstract: Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement's temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement's Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Quantum field theories provide fundamental models of complex interacting systems
                    1–3
                    , from high-energy physics and cosmology to condensed matter. However, solving these models in non-perturbative and dynamical regimes is often challenging, particularly in more than one spatial dimension. Analogue simulation using tunable synthetic quantum systems can both verify existing theoretical predictions and lead to physical insights. Here we realize analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time), using two coherently coupled spin components
                    4,5
                    in a uniform two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate
                    6,7
                    . Specifically, we encode the paradigmatic sine-Gordon model
                    8,9
                    in the long-wavelength modes of the field describing the relative phase,
                    ϕ
                    , of the two components. In the perturbative regime, collective field excitations exhibit a relativistic dispersion with a tunable mass gap. We also observe explicitly non-perturbative phenomena, including the existence of topological domain walls across which
                    ϕ
                    rapidly winds by 2π (ref.
                    10
                    ). Our work opens possibilities for studies of cosmologically relevant phenomena including preheating
                    11,12
                    , dynamics of topological defects
                    13,14
                    and relativistic false-vacuum decay
                    15–19
                    .

title: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies
abstract: The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder shows near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate-forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

title: Poxviruses probably evolved in the digestive system of animals
abstract: Large and giant DNA viruses that infect unicellular eukaryotes are abundant in the environment but have rarely been found in the gut microbiome. The discovery of such viruses that prevail in the digestive system of humans and animals exposes a long-overlooked facet of the gut microbiome that clarifies the origin of poxviruses. Newly discovered viruses distributed in animal digestive systems are the closest known relatives of the clade containing smallpox virus.

abstract: Thermal-shock catalysts, synthesized under non-equilibrium conditions through rapid heating to high temperatures followed by ultrafast cooling, represent a transformative class of materials. This Review discusses the use of thermal shock as a versatile non-equilibrium strategy for synthesizing single-atom, bimetallic, multi-elemental and other complex high-performance catalysts.

However, when a wound is large and the chemical becomes too concentrated, it attracts cannibalistic locusts. At low levels, guaiacol promotes immune function; at high levels, it prompts other locusts to eat their swarm-mate.

title: Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

title: Pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for systemic immune modulation in diabetes therapy
abstract: Embryonic development is characterized by remarkable immune tolerance, yet whether this property extends to pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) has remained unclear. Here we show that EVs from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), including embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells, outperform mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in suppressing proinflammatory cytokine secretion, reducing T cell activation and inducing regulatory T cells. PSC EVs display distinct molecular signatures, containing unique proteins and microRNAs absent from mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs, including the pluripotency-associated proteins ROR1 and CD133 and members of the miR-302 family. Dynamic suspension culture of PSC aggregates enhances the EV yield, providing a scalable and reproducible source. Delivered via a biomaterial scaffold, two local injections of induced PSC EVs significantly improved diabetes-free survival in an antigen-specific type 1 diabetes model, increasing regulatory T cell populations in draining lymph nodes, as well as inducing systemic immune modulation and preserving β-cell mass. These findings establish PSC EVs as a scalable immunomodulatory platform for autoimmune disease and for immune tolerance in cell therapy.

title: Dendrites trigger the alarm

abstract: Polyolefin upcycling is challenged by inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste. Here the authors show that common metal contaminants, particularly zeolite poisons such as Na, K, Ca, Mg and Cu, drive catalyst deactivation during cracking, while sulfur and chlorine are more benign. The catalyst remains active over extended operation and has the potential to yield cleaner pyrolysis oils than thermal pyrolysis.

title: An extracellular contractile injection system for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells
abstract: Protein delivery into plant cells remains a major barrier in plant biotechnology. The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC) is an extracellular contractile injection system, a phage tail-like bacterial nanomachine that naturally delivers proteins into insect host cells. Here we retargeted PVCs to plants by engineering their tail fibres to recognize the plant cell surface receptor FLAGELLIN SENSITIVE 2 (FLS2). We designed and characterized a library of FLS2-targeting PVCs and evaluated their ability to deliver native and non-native cargoes, including a fluorescent protein, Cre recombinase and R2 retroelement genome editor. Engineered PVCs delivered Cre into wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana benthamiana protoplasts and leaf cells with efficiencies up to 16%. Delivery was FLS2 dependent and scaled with receptor abundance, reaching 75% of leaf cells in FLS2-overexpressing Arabidopsis. We further demonstrated the PVC-mediated delivery of R2 protein, resulting in the targeted insertion of a reporter gene into the plant genome and the expression of the integrated gene. This work establishes PVCs as a platform for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells, laying the foundation for targeted and precise plant genetic engineering.

title: Designed broken symmetries facilitate configurational complexity in nematic vortex crystals
abstract:
Abstract
                  Although widely used in modern technological applications, liquid crystals have not yet been systematically explored or utilized as reconfigurable information storage devices. Here we demonstrate that precisely designed broken symmetries in nematic vortex crystal lattices give rise to exponential configurational complexity exceeding the configurational entropy of conventional atomic crystals, and arising from the manifold ways in which surface-anchored nematic defect lines can combine to form nematic vortex crystals with distinct free-energy minima and tailored broken symmetries, thereby generalizing the interstitial and substitutional defects as well as grain boundaries in conventional crystalline materials. We illustrate the versatility of our experimental platform by designing nematic vortex crystals with various broken symmetries and show how their topological states can be reconfigured on demand via laser-induced topological surgery. Thus, our results provide an experimental and conceptual foundation for the development of soft-matter-based topological memory and computation devices.

title: Visualizing surface restructuring and chemical state transitions in Co(OH)2 electrocatalysts during the oxygen evolution reaction
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Water splitting is a crucial component in sustainable energy conversion, with the oxygen evolution half-cell reaction (OER) remaining a major challenge. Rationalizing the morphological aspects underlying OER activity is complicated by restructuring and chemical state changes occurring concurrently on the catalyst’s surfaces. Here, using correlated atomic force, electron and X-ray microscopy during OER, we show that the restructuring of β-Co(OH)
                    2
                    nanoplates takes place together with the formation of Co oxide nanoparticles on the carbon support from leached Co species. Adding small amounts of Fe to the electrolyte not only results in the formation of a more active bimetallic nanoplate surface; it also partially hinders Co dissolution and results in a lower density of redeposited CoO
                    
                      x
                    
                    nanoparticles. These results emphasize how pre-catalyst restructuring and dissolution–redeposition during OER can combine to create active sites, and how subtle variations in reaction conditions and electrolyte composition can lead to distinctive catalyst morphologies and reactivities.

title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
abstract: The active transport and retention principle states that nanoparticles enter tumours via endothelial cells and exit via lymphatic drainage. How nanoparticles are retained in the tumour microenvironment remains unclear. Here we report a computational strategy to determine the mechanism of nanoparticle retention in solid tumours. We find that tumour cellular and acellular components delay and obstruct the movement of nanoparticles by influencing nanoparticle drag, Brownian and electric forces. We mathematically define nanoparticle retention based on these interactions, linking retention quantitatively to tumour pathophysiology, nanoparticle design and delivery efficiency. We create a software interface to simulate and predict nanoparticle retention across different tumour systems and nanoparticle designs, enabling us to select optimal tumour and nanoparticle delivery conditions for better therapeutic outcomes.

title: Retraction Note: Detection of anisotropic cosmic structures on a gigaparsec scale
Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination
abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

title: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
abstract: The economics of residential electrification in high-cost electricity regions remain uncertain. Using metered data from over 20,000 California homes, we assess the economic, environmental, and equity impacts of end-use electrification under rollout strategies based on household income and gas infrastructure age. Even under favorable electricity rates, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values (NPVs). Cost-effectiveness improves with deeper electrification scenarios, particularly when more costs are shifted to fixed charges and for homes with existing air conditioning—54–67% of these households break even when electrifying space heating, compared to fewer than 5% of those without. Income-based rebates more than double the share of low- and moderate-income households with positive NPVs. Prioritizing areas with aging gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions on par with high-income-led adoption and avoids costly pipeline replacement, but requires the highest subsidy to achieve cost-effectiveness across all households. These findings highlight trade-offs in designing equitable electrification strategies.

title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
abstract:
Abstract
                  Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. This enables a system-wide comparison of environmental impacts and resource requirements of global final energy provision from 2020 to 2100. We find that deep decarbonization delivers substantial cobenefits for human health and ecosystem quality, but does not systematically reduce pressures on land, water or mineral resource extraction. For metals central to electrification, climate change mitigation ambition primarily reshapes the timing of extraction rather than cumulative volumes. Pathways achieving similar climate targets can impose markedly different environmental and resource pressures, shaping the feasibility and desirability of alternative transitions.

title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
abstract: Mixed-matrix membranes promise to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, yet poor compatibility between the two limits their performance. New research shows that tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings, producing improved membranes for carbon capture.

title: Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
abstract: Antireflection coatings are widely used in optical systems to increase transmission and suppress unwanted reflections by matching the optical impedance across a uniform interface. Applying the same idea to metasurfaces is fundamentally more challenging because their wavefront control relies on arrays of geometrically distinct meta-atoms, presenting as a spatially varying optical impedance. Here we show that vertical integration can overcome this limitation by allowing bilayer meta-atoms to act simultaneously as phase shifters and impedance-matching stacks. By treating meta-atoms as multilayer thin films, we derive a design rule that links the effective refractive indices of two independently patterned layers and identifies antireflective bilayer libraries with full 0-2π transmission phase coverage. We demonstrate the approach with a free-standing TiO2/TiO2 metalens operating at 1,310 nm, which suppresses reflection below that of bare glass while maintaining diffraction-limited focusing. These results establish bilayer metasurfaces as a platform for jointly engineering optical impedance and wavefront response at the meta-atom level.

title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
abstract: Linking electrode microstructure to electrochemical performance is essential for optimizing Li-ion batteries. However, this requires mechanistic four-dimensional observations at the ultimate spatiotemporal scales, which remain elusive. Here we demonstrate the use of interrupted-operando synchrotron X-ray nano-holotomography combined with digital volume correlation to track chemomechanical dynamics at both particle (local) and electrode (averaged) scales. Quantitative scale-bridging image analysis is applied to composite graphite-silicon electrodes during their electrochemical formation cycle. Our findings reveal that local ionic diffusion properties, graphite particle morphology and position in the electrode, distance to silicon clusters, surface contact with the liquid electrolyte solution, and mechanical deformations all directly affect local electrochemical activity and irreversibility, although these parameters are not equally important. In particular, we identify fast ionic diffusion channels that play a key role and counterbalance intrinsic depth-dependent reaction heterogeneities arising from ionic and electronic diffusion limitations. The various structural factors that determine the electrochemical performance of composite graphite-silicon electrodes in Li-ion batteries beyond ensemble properties are classified using a scale of influence, providing a practical framework for the optimization of materials and electrode manufacturing.

title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes
abstract: Oxoboranes, compounds featuring a central dicoordinate boron atom engaged in a B–O triple bond, have long been regarded as highly reactive and are typically observed only as transient species. Although attempts to synthesize them date back to the 1960s, their isolation in the condensed phase has proved challenging. Now, two independent studies describe the isolation of neutral and cationic oxoboranes derived from related diboracumulenes.

title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
abstract: High energy density promised by solid-state batteries requires overcoming fundamental limitations in carrier transport. Although tortuous carrier pathways in high-loading cathodes are often viewed as the dominant bottleneck, we show that interfacial ion and electron transport is an even more critical lever for enhancing energy density in sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries. By enabling partial lithiation at the sulfur-sulfide interface and eliminating the electron-impeding oxidation layer at the sulfur-carbon interface, we achieve high-loading all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery cathodes with areal capacities near 15 mAh cm-2 and sulfur utilization above 90% with a moderate stack pressure of 15-25 MPa. These metrics correspond to projected pouch-cell-level energy densities surpassing 500 Wh kg-1. Fast cycling at 1C retains 82.1% capacity over 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiencies up to 99.9%, and stable cycling is also achieved with a lithium metal anode at 10 MPa instead of the more common Li-In alloy. This work highlights the power of interfacial control within composite cathodes, and demonstrates another approach for designing high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries for next-generation energy storage.

title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Conjugated molecular belts attract increasing attention because of the unusual electronic and magnetic behaviour arising from their radially oriented
                    p
                    orbitals. A π-conjugated molecular belt is expected to behave like a quantum ring, showing global aromatic or antiaromatic ring currents, but in most hydrocarbon benzenoid belts, localized Clar sextets preclude the emergence of global ring currents. Here we report the synthesis of anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts that sustain global antiaromatic ring currents in the neutral state. Macrocyclization was achieved by nickel(0)-mediated Yamamoto coupling. Scholl oxidation with DDQ/TfOH, promoted by electron-donating methoxy substituents, yielded the strained triple-stranded nanobelts. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons, as revealed by
                    1
                    H NMR spectroscopy and corroborated by computational analysis. This work establishes a platform for synthesizing other heterocyclic nanobelts, in cases where the corresponding hydrocarbon nanobelt is not yet synthetically accessible.

title: Climate and glacier geometry dominate global glacier–lake interactions
abstract: The contribution of glacial lakes to glacier mass loss is unclear. This work maps global glacial lakes in 2000 and 2020 to quantify changes in number, volume and area, showing that they explain 11 ± 7% of lake-terminating glacier loss, with climate forcing and glacier geometry the dominant factors.

title: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: How do our brains manage to store our everyday experiences into memory? Neurons in the human temporal lobe that respond to the concept of an individual person or object have been shown to provide the semantic building blocks for episodic memory. Recording from 1415 neurons in neurosurgical patients who learned a story involving specific concepts, we found reactivation of neurons representing these concepts during slow-wave sleep after learning. Concept neurons were conjointly reactivated, particularly during sharp-wave ripples, with time lags suitable for synaptic modification. However, the temporal sequence of reactivation did not reflect the sequence of concepts in the learned story. Unlike rodent place cells, which can acquire preferred firing locations during exploration of new environments according to their pre-existing preferred sequence of activation, human concept neurons are tuned to specific semantic contents before learning starts. Consequently, pre-existing firing sequences correlate with consecutive place fields in rodents, but not with sequences of events in human experience. Thus, in contrast to reactivation of rodent place cells, reactivation of human concept cells does not reflect sequences of events in human experience.

title: Technology trajectories and critical raw materials in sodium-ion battery innovation: An LLM-assisted patent analysis
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising complement to lithium-ion batteries for cost-sensitive and resource-resilient energy-storage applications. Despite growing technological and industrial interest, the structure of SIB innovation remains insufficiently understood because existing patent studies have largely focused on aggregate filing trends. To address this gap, this study develops a high-resolution patent landscape through large language model-assisted classification of 9670 patent families across technological domains, battery components, electrode material classes, assignee types, regions, and cathode-related critical raw materials. The results show that SIB innovation remains strongly materials-driven, with material-related inventions accounting for almost 86% of all patent families. Within this landscape, layered transition-metal oxides account for 51% of cathode-related patent families, while hard carbon represents 44% of anode-related patent families. Innovation activity is also highly concentrated geographically, with more than 94% of the analyzed patent families including at least one Chinese assignee. At the organizational level, companies focus more strongly on near-term material pathways, whereas public organizations show greater engagement with alternative chemistries. Furthermore, critical raw materials (CRMs) continue to play a central role in SIB cathodes: 76% of cathode patent families require at least one CRM, 15% include one conditionally, and only 9% contain no CRM. The degree of this exposure varies substantially across cathode classes, with manganese, nickel, phosphorus, and vanadium emerging as the most prominent CRMs. Overall, these findings show that the strategic value of SIBs depends on material selection, regional innovation capacity, and chemistry-specific CRM exposure, with implications for research, industry, and policy.

title: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The auditory brainstem implant (ABI) targeting the cochlear nucleus (CN) can restore hearing in patients ineligible for cochlear implants. However, conventional ABI using surface electrode array yields highly variable outcomes, from poor to moderate, due to limited spatial resolution and restricted tonotopic access. Here, we developed a penetrating ABI based on a high-density, ultra-flexible implantable neural electrode array (uFINE). In normal-hearing rats, uFINE mapped frequency tuning from 0.5 to 32 kHz in CN and the inferior colliculus (IC). Selective CN stimulation via uFINE evoked IC responses closely matching acoustic tonotopy, with IC tuning widths comparable to tone-evoked responses, and these remained stable for over 136 days, with minimal gliosis observed. Daily sequential CN–IC microstimulation progressively shifted the location of the CN-evoked IC response peak toward the targeted IC stimulation site, consistent with use-dependent plasticity. Together, these findings demonstrate that uFINE enables high-resolution, tonotopically precise, and long-term stable CN stimulation across a broad frequency range with minimal tissue disruption, highlighting its potential to enhance ABI-mediated hearing restoration.

title: Heparan sulfate sulfatases are essential for the patterning of human stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Midbrain dopaminergic neurons (mDA) are selectively lost in Parkinson’s disease, driving sustained efforts to generate bona fide mDA neurons from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) for replacement therapy. While morphogen gradients and transcription factors have been extensively studied, extracellular regulators remain largely overlooked. Here, we identify the heparan sulfate-modifying enzymes SULF1 and SULF2 as essential for establishing mDA neuron identity in vitro. Using CRISPR/Cas9-engineered iPSCs, we show that loss of SULF1/2 increases 6-O-sulfated heparan sulfate species and disrupts patterning both at the anteroposterior and dorsoventral axes in human iPSC-derived mDA cultures. Double-knockout cells thus fail to acquire ventral midbrain fates and instead adopt hindbrain, spinal cord and neural crest-like identities as revealed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Mechanistically, we partially explain the changed patterning to aberrant FGF signaling and demonstrate that FGF inhibition redirects cells toward midbrain fates, however without restoring ventral identity. These findings establish a critical role for SULF1/2 in mDA neuron in vitro differentiation and uncover a previously unrecognized layer of extracellular control over neural patterning.

title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. Using 259,732 phenological observations across eight European woody species spanning 1950–2024, we show that foliar frost damage shortened the fruit development period (FDP; the interval from flowering to fruit maturity) by 1.6 days, driven by delayed flowering and advanced fruit maturity. Conversely, floral frost damage prolonged FDP by 1.3 days through delayed fruit maturity, with both effects strengthening under greater frost severity. Accounting for anomalously warm conditions in the frost year substantially reduced the estimated delays in flowering and subsequent-year phenology, indicating that neglecting climatic context leads to overestimation of frost effects. These findings reveal organ-specific pathways through which frost damage reshapes reproductive phenology while generating limited carry-over effects, refining current understanding of phenological responses under climate change.

title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although desmin intermediate filaments are critical for muscle architecture and homeostasis, their spatial 3D organization remains elusive. Their known localization to sarcomeric Z-lines delimits the periodic array of actin and myosin filaments. Here, using dSTORM and SIM sub-diffraction resolution microscopy, we resolve the spatial 3D organization of desmin filaments within mouse skeletal muscle, and reveal they are not confined to Z-lines. Our reconstruction reveals that desmin intermediate filaments extend from Z-lines into the sarcomere interior, where they align with actin filaments. Functional assays show that disrupting desmin filament assembly in normal male mouse muscle using a dominant negative inhibitor of desmin selectively reduces active tension at longer sarcomere lengths, indicating a role for desmin in sarcomere mechanics. These findings expand the structural model of the muscle sarcomere and support a role for desmin in force production.

title: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Benzoxaboroles (BoBs) such as acoziborole feature a boron-heterocyclic core and are an important innovation in the development of drugs against a range of pathogens and other pathologies. A broad pharmacological spectrum is associated with chemically diverse BoB derivatives, including multiple modes-of-action (MoA) and molecular targets. However, a consensus MoA for BoBs targeting evolutionarily diverse protozoan pathogens has emerged, with identification of CPSF3 in the CPSF complex as a target in both apicomplexan and kinetoplastida parasites. Here, using comprehensive genetic screens in Trypanosoma brucei, we establish a functional connection between the boron-heterocyclic scaffold shared by all BoBs and protein sumoylation genes. We observe a rapid, transient increase in global protein sumoylation following BoB exposure. While we do not observe direct CPSF3 sumoylation, we find that acoziborole and other BoBs rapidly and specifically destabilise CPSF3 in a SUMO- and proteasome-dependent manner.

title: A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The genome-wide binding patterns of many transcription factors (TFs) depend not only on the presence of their recognition motifs, but also on the surrounding chromatin context. This raises the question of how binding specificity, which is essential for the proper activation of regulatory regions during development and differentiation, is achieved. Two competing hypotheses have been proposed: either opening is a hierarchical process, whereby chromatin-insensitive TFs bind initially and render the DNA accessible for the subsequent binding of other TFs, or multiple chromatin-sensitive TFs bind cooperatively, enabling them to overcome the chromatin barrier. Here, we provide a quantitative framework to assess the chromatin sensitivity of individual TFs, and demonstrate that it generally depends on motif strength and is a continuum across TFs. This indicates that regulatory regions are activated by neither a purely hierarchical nor a purely cooperative mechanism, but rather by a mixture of both mechanisms, in a locus-specific manner.

title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Radical glycosylation offers versatile strategies for carbohydrate synthesis, yet the development of accessible glycosyl radical precursors compatible with stereoselective coupling remains challenging. Here we report a nickel-catalysed stereoselective denitrogenative glycosylation of redox-neutral glycosyl sulfonohydrazides via anomeric C–N bond homolysis. Bench-stable (un)protected glycosyl sulfonohydrazides are concisely and catalytically synthesized via an open–closed ring equilibrium without stoichiometric reagents, and intrinsically generate glycosyl radicals without external redox additives, offering remarkable practical utility. This operationally simple, nickel-catalysed denitrogenative glycosylation platform, proceeding without photocatalysis, enables highly stereoselective formation of diverse C(sp³)–C(sp³), C(sp³)–C(sp²), C(sp³)–C(sp), C(sp³)–S, C(sp³)–Se, and C(sp³)–Te bonds, with broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Mechanistic studies support a radical pathway involving Ni(II)–isodiazene homolysis and thermal N₂ extrusion. This work establishes glycosyl sulfonohydrazides as an interesting class of N-based glycosyl radical precursors, expanding the “cap-and-glycosylate” strategy for glycomimetic synthesis and glycodiversification.

title: Electrically induced glass transition of polyelectrolyte complexes enables kinetic ionic diodes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The glass transition induces pronounced changes in material properties, transforming a rigid glass into a soft rubber. Here, we demonstrate an electrically induced glass transition in a polyelectrolyte complex (PEC), sandwiched between two oppositely charged ionoelastomers (IEs). Under an external electric potential, the IEs reversibly inject and extract their counter-ions into and from the PECs, triggering a glass transition in accordance with the time-temperature-salt superposition (TTSS) principle. Reversible, real-time switching of the glass transition at voltages as low as 1 V induces changes in ionic conductivity of the PEC, enabling kinetically driven ionic current rectification.

title: Super-resolution microscopy reveals distinct epigenetic states regulated by estrogen receptor activity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Changes in gene expression regulated by ligand-dependent transcription factors including estrogen receptor-α (ERα) involve coactivator recruitment and H3K27ac deposition. While H3K27ac marks active enhancers, the chromatin architecture of enhancers remains unclear. Using super-resolution microscopy, we reveal distinct H3K27ac-modified chromatin structures in response to ERα activation. Estradiol (E2) treatment promotes elongated H3K27ac structures, whereas ERα inhibition induces compact, spherical conformations. Larger H3K27ac structures show greater MED1 association than compact structures, indicating distinct spatial relationships with enhancer-associated transcriptional machinery. Spatial analyses revealed that estrogen signaling reorganizes H3K27ac into densely packed nanoscale territories enriched for larger domains. Complementary genomic and transcriptomic analyses showed that broader H3K27ac regulatory regions are associated with MED1 occupancy and increased transcriptional output. The endocrine therapy-resistant ERα Y537S mutation maintains elongated chromatin states independent of ligand. These findings uncover the -spatial dimension of H3K27ac chromatin organization in ERα-responsive and endocrine-resistant breast cancer.

title: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Stature is a key indicator of pediatric health, yet the molecular and metabolic architecture governing childhood growth remains incompletely defined. We conduct genome-wide association analyses of stature from birth to childhood (574,580 measurements; 72,704 Norwegian children) and integrate UK Biobank data (age 10 and adulthood). We uncover life-stage shifts in the genetics of stature, identifying previously not identified childhood-specific effects including variants near GLP1R with BMI-independent effects, and reveal three temporal clusters - Infancy and Childhood clusters enriched for endocrine and metabolic pathways, and a Lifetime growth cluster enriched for skeletal biology. Proteome analysis reveals that prepubertal height is associated with widespread changes in the circulation, identifying 106 height-associated proteins and linking IGF1, IGF2, and IGFBP3 levels to childhood-height polygenic scores. Mendelian randomization shows that reduced fetal growth and taller prepubertal height increase type 2 diabetes risk, independent of adult stature. These findings uncover developmental stage-specific genetic and proteomic influences on child-growth and links to adult metabolic health.

title: Good Practices and Common Pitfalls in the Research and Development of New Electrolytes for Flow Batteries
abstract: Abstract Redox flow batteries represent one of the most actively investigated platforms for grid-scale electrochemical energy storage. The rapid expansion of electrolyte chemistries has broadened the field, but has also introduced significant inconsistencies in experimental methods, testing protocols, and reporting practices. This variability impedes interlaboratory comparison and, in some cases, produces misleading assessments of electrolyte performance and stability. This article presents structured, practical guidance for researchers working with novel flow battery electrolytes, organized around four core activities: electrolyte formulation and physicochemical characterization, electroanalytical screening, flow cell assembly and hardware selection, and performance and lifetime evaluation. Key topics include staged characterization of redox-active compounds from dilute cyclic voltammetry through operationally relevant conditions, component selection and compatibility checks, the distinction between symmetric and full cell configurations for performance versus lifetime testing, and the role of potentiostatic cycling protocols in generating reliable capacity fade data. Finally, the reporting of capacity fade is discussed with consideration of the underlying degradation mechanisms. The guidance is condensed into ten practical recommendations, and the article is published as a living document on GitHub, open to continuous community revision and peer review to work toward a community consensus on experimental and reporting practices in our field.

title: Molten‐Salt Surface Restructuring of 3D‐Printed Agitator Exposes Ni 0 Active Sites for Efficient Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
abstract: ABSTRACT Three‐dimensional (3D) printing enables the integration of structural engineering with catalytic functionality, yet extending this concept to high‐pressure liquid‐phase hydrogenation remains challenging because catalytic efficiency, selectivity, and structural robustness are difficult to optimize simultaneously. Here, we report a strategy that couples additive manufacturing with molten‐salt activation to engineer a 3D‐printed bladed agitator catalyst (AB–MSL–H 2 ). Molten‐salt treatment selectively reconstructs the alloy surface while preserving the printed architecture, generating a Ni‐enriched interface with abundant exposed metallic Ni 0 active sites. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that surface reconstruction enriches accessible Ni 0 sites to direct the desired hydrogenation pathway while suppressing isomerization, cyclization, and hydrogenolysis, whereas the integrated bladed architecture simultaneously enhances gas‐liquid‐solid mass transfer and reactant accessibility. Consequently, AB–MSL–H 2 achieves complete conversion of 2‐butyne‐1,4‐diol with a 1,4‐butanediol yield exceeding 97%. This work establishes a general strategy for transforming additively manufactured structural alloys into catalytically active reactor components through molten‐salt‐induced surface reconstruction, expanding the scope of catalyst‐reactor integration for high‐pressure liquid‐phase catalysis.

title: Indirect Characterization of 14 N Nuclei via 1 H‐Detected Rotating‐Frame Relaxometry
abstract: ABSTRACT 14 N NMR is notoriously difficult to perform in liquids due to the very fast spin relaxation and the large quadrupolar couplings, which render many signals invisible. We show here how 14 N nuclei of biomolecular constituents can be probed indirectly by reintroducing the scalar relaxation of the second kind contribution as a relaxation pathway for J‐coupled protons in double resonance spin‐locking experiments. The enhanced 1 H relaxation rates in the rotating‐frame allow for direct evaluation of nitrogen chemical shifts and polarization lifetimes, from which one‐ and even two‐bond 1 H‐ 14 N scalar couplings as well as 14 N quadrupolar interactions can be determined. We demonstrate the versatility of this method by characterizing 1 H‐ 14 N spin pairs in several molecules of biological importance, showing proton relaxation enhancements beyond one order of magnitude. We further observe a pronounced effect from intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Our approach can be readily integrated into existing liquid‐state NMR methodologies, as demonstrated here for 1 H‐detected relaxation‐editing experiments with water suppression. This method provides access to nitrogen's picosecond‐modulated quadrupolar interaction via sensitive proton detection in systems that would otherwise yield almost no detectable direct 14 N signal even after averaging over thousands of transients.

title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I 2 ) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole‐transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine‐trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium‐based interfacial modifiers, PTZ‐PEFAI and PXZ‐PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy‐level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I 2 through halogen bonding, enabling I 2 capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I 3 − in modifier‐iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine‐vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p‐type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy‐level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ‐PEFAI‐treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a T 85 lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial iodine chemistry and charge transport toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Atomic‐Scale Origin of Charge Density Wave–Driven Metal–Semiconductor Transition in an Incommensurately Modulated Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Although metal–organic frameworks are widely recognized for their long‐range crystalline periodicity, they can also exhibit intrinsic aperiodic structures associated with incommensurate modulation, whose observation has been exceptionally rare. In low‐dimensional condensed matter physics, these unique structures often give rise to novel physical phenomena such as charge density wave. However, owing to limited direct experimental evidence, the relationship between incommensurate structural modulation and temperature‐dependent electronic transport in conductive metal–organic frameworks remains incompletely understood. Here, using high‐quality Pr 3 HHTP 2 (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) single crystals as a model system, we resolve the incommensurately modulated structure at 100 K (modulation vector q = 0.39143(12) c * ) via temperature‐dependent single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction. The observed reversible metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K occurs in a similar temperature range to the disappearance of the structural modulation, supporting a connection between lattice distortion and electronic behavior. The modulation reappears upon cooling, with guest water molecules influencing both the extent of its recovery and the electrical conductivity of the material. This work establishes a concrete experimental criterion for one‐dimensional charge density wave in metal‐organic frameworks and provides an ideal platform for probing coupled electronic–lattice modulations.

title: Precisely Recyclable, Multifunctional, and High‐Performance Polyester Integrated by a Single Imidazolium‐Monomer
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable lifecycle management of polymer materials urgently requires integrating green synthesis, service‐stage desired properties, and end‐of‐life easy recyclability. Herein, by introducing a single imidazolium‐monomer, the all‐in‐one integration of green preparation (without solvents or additives), multifunctionality (flame retardancy and antistatic property), high performance (excellent chromaticity, high heat resistance and high strength), and precise recyclability (in mixed wastes) for polyesters is achieved, which also reduces the health risks caused by additive migration. The key is that the imidazolium unit can not only control the C(alkyl)─O cleavage at high temperature to hinder polyester combustion but also catalyze the C(carbonyl)─O cleavage at the ester site to achieve chemical recycling of polyester. Without halogen or phosphorus elements, the polyester exhibits excellent chromaticity (L* value > 89 and b* value 11 Ω), flame retardancy (the best UL‐94 V‐0 rating) and precise recycling in extremely complex mixed polymer wastes. This work successfully achieves lifecycle management of polyester materials via a single imidazolium‐monomer, providing a feasible platform for the next generation of sustainable, multifunctional and high‐performance polymer materials.

title: Biomimetic N ‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT Homologation is a key tactic used in the lead optimization of small‐molecule pharmaceuticals due to the potent impact such modifications can have on target affinity and physicochemical properties. However, while many elegant homologation strategies have been developed for the synthesis of β 3 ‐amino acids via decarboxylation, preparation of the β 2 ‐amino acid homologues remains underexplored. We report a general biomimetic strategy for the N ‐terminal homologation of amino acids using photoredox catalysis. Key to the success of this approach is a radical translocation cascade driven by single‐electron transfer. This methodology provides streamlined access to a range of cyclic and acyclic β 2 ‐amino acids and phosphonates, providing new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.

title: Interfacial Molecular Engineering Mediated Intramolecular Inter‐Group Relay Effect Enables Efficient Acidic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic media represents an attractive strategy for improving carbon utilization efficiency by suppressing carbonate formation. However, achieving highly selective C 2+ products at high current densities remains a formidable challenge due to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and sluggish C─C coupling process. Here, we introduce the surface‐adsorbed bifunctional organic molecule on Cu (Cu─SBMA), which delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 90.4% for C 2+ products at 0.8 A cm −2 under acid media and pure CO 2 flow, together with a single‐pass carbon efficiency (SPCE) of 92.8% at 0.6 A cm −2 . Furthermore, under diluted CO 2 flow (15 vol% CO 2 ), Cu─SBMA still maintains a high C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 85.3% at 0.4 A cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy and DFT calculations uncover an intramolecular inter‐group relay mechanism that governs asymmetrical OC─CHO coupling toward C 2+ productions. Specifically, the quaternary ammonium (─N + (CH 3 ) 2 ─) group promotes CO 2 activation and stabilizes *CO intermediate, the adjacent sulfonate (SO 3 − ) moiety mediates protonation of *CO toward *CHO. The intramolecular inter‐group relay effect facilitates C─C coupling and suppresses HER. Our findings provide novel insights for the precise design of catalysts to regulate the reaction selectivity of complex multi‐step energy conversion process.

title: Solvent‐Removal‐Induced Lattice Reconstruction Enables Tunable Mn 2+ Luminescence in Hybrid [MnBr 4 ] 2− for 3D X‐Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT It is challenging to understand how noncoordinating lattice guests regulate Mn 2+ luminescence without changing the metal coordination environment. Herein, we report a solvent‐removal‐induced single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal (SCSC) transformation from ethanol‐containing (C 33 H 29 NP) 2 MnBr 4 ·EtOH (CZTPPM) to the solvent‐free phase (C 33 H 29 NP) 2 MnBr 4 (CZTPPM1). Ethanol removal preserves the configuration of isolated [MnBr 4 ] 2− tetrahedra while inducing lattice contraction, hydrogen‐bonding network reorganization, and enhanced tetrahedral distortion. As a result, the emission undergoes a distinct green (518 nm) to yellow‐green (543 nm) shift. Combined low‐temperature excitation spectroscopy, crystal‐field analysis, electron‐phonon coupling evaluation, and excited‐state decay kinetics establish a correlation between supramolecular lattice reconstruction, local ligand‐field modulation, and excited‐state relaxation. Furthermore, the solvent‐free phase retains efficient scintillation performance (including light yield of 56, 516 photons MeV −1 and detection limit of 59.97 nGy air s −1 ) and enables high‐resolution static X‐ray imaging and 3D X‐ray reconstruction. This work provides insight into noncoordinating‐guest‐mediated crystal‐field regulation and demonstrates its potential for developing multifunctional luminescent materials for radiation imaging.

title: Dual‐DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi‐DUB Engagement
abstract: ABSTRACT Targeted protein stabilization has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring the abundance and function of disease‐relevant proteins. Deubiquitinase‐targeting chimeras (DUBTACs) offer a chemical approach to protein stabilization by recruiting deubiquitinases (DUBs) to promote target deubiquitination. However, current DUBTAC strategies generally rely on the recruitment of a single DUB, leaving the potential of engaging multiple DUBs through a common recruiter largely unexplored. Here, we report a dual‐DUBTAC strategy that enables targeted protein stabilization through the recruitment of two distinct DUBs. Using Degrasyn, a small‐molecule reversible covalent inhibitor of multiple DUBs, as a privileged scaffold, we engineered small molecules that selectively stabilize CFTR and cGAS and demonstrate that these compounds enhance target protein homeostasis through USP9X‐ and USP5‐mediated deubiquitination in cells. By decoupling substrate stabilization from reliance on a single DUB, the Dual‐DUB platform confers adaptability across diverse ubiquitin chain architectures and rewired proteostasis networks characteristic of heterogeneous tumors and could overcome potential drug resistance in future clinical applications. This strategy expands the chemical space for restoring protective proteins and establishes a general framework for functional reactivation of destabilized tumor‐suppressive pathways.

title: Cryptochiral Circularly Polarized Luminescence Emerges From Cosolvent‐Regulated Pathway Complexity in Amyloidogenic Peptide Self‐Assembly
abstract: ABSTRACT Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is important for chiral photonics, optical encryption, bioimaging, and information processing. It is usually associated with an identifiable chiral ground‐state organization, and CPL without detectable ground‐state chirality remains comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report a rare “ cryptochiral CPL ” phenomenon arising from cosolvent‐regulated pathway complexity in the self‐assembly of a naphthalimide (NMI)‐amyloidogenic peptide conjugate (PEP‐L). In water, PEP‐L spontaneously forms thermodynamically stable, emissive nanofibers with pronounced supramolecular chirality and strong CPL. Adding a small amount of cosolvent redirects assembly toward kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies and shows no detectable Circular Dichroism (CD) response in the naphthalimide chromophore region, but retains pronounced CPL, which decouples ground‐state and excited‐state chiroptical responses. We term this behavior cryptochiral CPL . Thermal annealing or aging converts the spheres into thermodynamically favored nanofibers with distinct CD and CPL characteristics. The enantiomer PEP‐D shows mirror‐image chiroptical responses, which validates the phenomenon. Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under different conditions give molecular‐level insight into the conformation, noncovalent interactions, and supramolecular organization of the different assembly states. These findings establish a new conceptual framework for adaptive chiral photonic materials and open opportunities for hidden optical encoding and biomolecular photonic systems.

title: Entropy‐Compensated Electrolyte Enables Low‐Temperature 400 Wh Kg −1 Silicon‐Based Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolytes dictate the low‐temperature (LT) performance of Si‐anode lithium‐ion batteries, wherein bulk solvation governs Li + transport and interfacial stability. Especially, enlarged ionic clusters and strengthened ion pairing at LT hinder Li + migration, limiting Li + supply to the interface and destabilizing interfacial reactions. Herein, we propose an entropy‐compensation strategy to counteract LT‐induced solvation deterioration in Si‐anode electrolytes. Increasing the solvation entropy ( ΔS solv ) compensates for the LT‐induced increase in the Gibbs free‐energy change for ion‐cluster dissociation ( ΔG solv ), thereby raising the corresponding equilibrium constant ( K solv ) and suppressing ion pairing. Consequently, electrolytes preferentially form smaller anion‐rich ionic clusters, delivering an approximately threefold increase in ionic conductivity at −20°C. Enhanced bulk transport alleviates concentration polarization, stabilizes the interfacial solvation environment, and promotes uniform SEI‐forming reactions. Benefiting from this coupled bulk‐interfacial optimization, Ah‐level pouch cells retain 97.8% capacity after 165 cycles at −20°C and support sustained discharge at −81°C. This strategy enables high‐energy pouch cells to deliver 400 Wh kg −1 under ambient conditions and 339 Wh kg −1 at LT, while an Ah‐level pouch cell retains 80% capacity after 1150 cycles at 2 C. This work identifies ΔS solv as a critical thermodynamic descriptor for low‐temperature electrolyte design.

title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics
abstract: ABSTRACT The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe 2 nanoclusters onto MoSe 2 piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal‐support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long‐lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d‐band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g −1 with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe 2 . Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g −1 with stable long‐term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni SA ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H 2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ + ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d‐p orbital hybridization between Ni SA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni SA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni SA ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H 2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h −1 g −1 . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high‐performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

title: Photoreduction of Chlorinated Volatile Waste Into C 2+ Hydrocarbons
abstract: ABSTRACT Chlorinated volatile organic compounds (Cl─VOCs) are a class of major environmental pollutants and potential human carcinogens. Dechlorination of Cl─VOC waste into harmless and value‐added chemicals under mild conditions is highly desirable yet challenging, and cannot be achieved using current photocatalytic methods. Here, we report the synthesis of the first nickel anthraquinone–thiolate complex for photoreduction of a variety of Cl─VOCs into unsaturated C 2+ hydrocarbons in good yields using visible light. Notably, the molecular system is capable of both reducing C 2 Cl─VOCs with high chlorine content into acetylene and C─C coupling of C 1 Cl─VOCs into ethylene and propylene. Mechanistic studies reveal that multielectron and multi‐proton reduction of the nickel complex is critical in generating the catalytically active species for various reductive dechlorination transformations. This study provides a blueprint for the conversion of chlorinated waste into highly valuable chemicals using solar energy.

title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less‐colored states upon heating due to disruption of π‐conjugation. In contrast, heat‐triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation‐switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone‐functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li + , Na + , and Ag + ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible‐ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li + /PF 6 − ion‐pair‐cooperation‐promoted ring‐opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal‐ion‐regulated conjugation‐switching strategy for heat‐activated colorless‐to‐colored switching and responsive optical materials.

title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Ether‐oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether‐oxygen groups into high‐connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]‐connected 3D COFs with scu topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight‐connected ether‐oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high‐stability light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether‐oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni‐incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2‐aminobenzenethiol to produce 2‐phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas‐phase H 2 product (∼1.15 mmol g −1 h −1 ). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale‐up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

title: Advancing C3 Polymerization of Alkynylcyclopropanes via a Synergistic Lewis Acid/Brønsted Base/C(sp 3 )–H Bond System
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of cyclopropane chemistry with polymer science could offer access to unique all‐carbon polymers. However, the ring‐opening polymerization (ROP) of cyclopropanes generally requires strong electron‐donating and ‐withdrawing substituents, limiting the use of electronically less activated monomers such as 2‐alkynylcyclopropane‐1,1‐dicarboxylates (ACPs). Here, we demonstrate that the synergistic combination of a Lewis acid and a Brønsted base overcomes the electronic limitations imposed by carbon–carbon triple bonds, including their high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability, enabling the unprecedented C3 ROP of ACPs. This process is regulated by a reversible‐deactivation equilibrium mediated by chain‐end C(sp 3 )─H bonds, affording well‐defined polymers bearing alkyne side groups. The resulting functional polymers provide a versatile platform for applications ranging from stimulus‐responsive sensing to Raman imaging.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
abstract: ABSTRACT The protolignin standardization transformation into high‐value‐added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3‐alkyl guaiacol (C3‐G), stoichiometric diazotization‐reductive ammonification of C3‐G to aminophenol C3‐GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3‐GAP to the benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor‐selective cytotoxicity of the as‐synthesized G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3‐GLB‐pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high‐value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO 2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon dioxide (CO 2 )‐derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO 2 ‐based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequences.
