Operating-point-dependent power-flow linearisation for joint siting, sizing, and dispatch of long-duration energy storage in distribution grids
abstract: Long-term energy-storage planning in distribution grids involves long time series, non-linear network constraints, and mixed-integer siting and sizing decisions. Especially detailed AC formulations are computationally challenging for long optimisation horizons. To address this challenge, we propose an operating-point-dependent linearisation of the AC power-flow equations using sensitivity coefficients and integrating them into a mixed-integer linear program for the joint siting, sizing and dispatch of different flexibility options over long time horizons. An iterative AC power-flow validation and relinearisation procedure is used to ensure approximation accuracy. Different approaches to select the linearisation points are benchmarked, either by using each operating point or by clustering approaches, using k -medoids while retaining the original injection and network data. The method is evaluated on SimBench distribution networks and benchmarked against non-linear AC-OPF formulations. Operating-point-dependent linearisation enables computationally tractable storage planning over long time horizons while preserving detailed network information. Clustering can reduce computational effort by about 40 % , provided that the original operating-point data are retained. The linearised model deviates from the lossless AC-OPF benchmark by approximately 0.3 % in storage power and 0.6 % in energy capacity. To demonstrate the use of the method, we develop a case study where household flexibility and grid scale storage are co-optimised in a full-year planning problem. The results show that aggregate household flexibility primarily affects storage sizing, whereas its spatial distribution influences local grid conditions and optimal siting.

title: Stochastic assessment of eight emergency electricity supply configurations for urban shelters: Performance limits and the role of vehicle-to-shelter
abstract: Emergency electricity planning for urban shelters requires comparing heterogeneous supply resources under uncertain, time-varying demand. This study assesses eight specified emergency electricity-supply configurations, including two Vehicle-to-Shelter (V2S) arrangements, for a 1000-person shelter during a 72-h grid outage. A common framework combines paired Monte Carlo simulation, hourly supply–demand matching, continuous resource-state evolution, and access-conditioned variance decomposition, while retaining configuration-specific constraints on power, usable energy, infrastructure continuity, resource access, and deployment timing. Across nine demand and disaster-severity scenarios, adequacy declined as shelter services expanded and cold-season demand increased, while access-dependent resources were additionally constrained by infrastructure continuity, allocation, and arrival. High coverage of the specified diesel-generator configuration depended strongly on its usable energy in the most demanding scenario, where a 20% stock reduction lowered mean energy coverage ratio (ECR) from 0.819 to 0.659. Similar aggregate coverage also concealed different temporal risks. Under hot conditions with moderate disaster severity, a mobile power-supply truck and a local-plus-external V2S arrangement had nearly identical mean ECRs (0.368 and 0.367) under baseline access assumptions but different temporal shortfall patterns. The truck provided no support before allocation and arrival, whereas locally parked EVs supplied limited early power. Access-state differences accounted for most observed ECR variance for the access-dependent configurations in the two examined scenarios, distinguishing conditional resource capability from unconditional shelter adequacy. These findings support mechanism-based screening by power, endurance, immediate availability, and credible access arrangements, while suggesting a potential role for V2S as a conditional supplement rather than a universal substitute for dedicated backup supply.

title: A continental dilemma: Is centralized or decentralized renewable hydrogen cheaper?
abstract: Hydrogen is a strong candidate on the path towards the decarbonization of the transportation, energy, and industry sectors. In addition to being a well-known element, hydrogen is mainly produced from fossil fuels, with the renewable production chain still requiring development. In this context, this work evaluates the technical and economic potential of hydrogen production using solar photovoltaic (PV) energy and electricity purchased from the Brazilian grid, and evaluates two layouts: (i) centralized production of solar PV energy and hydrogen at the same site and (ii) decentralized production of energy and hydrogen powered by the Brazilian interconnected grid (SIN). The use of PV energy is found to decrease the levelized cost of hydrogen ( L C O H ) when compressed, from 14.00 USD / kg to 13.24 USD / kg in the centralized case and to 9.11 USD / kg in the decentralized case. However, a system powered only by P V energy had a cost of 18.23 USD / kg ; this corroborates the fact that the highest verified cost is from the purchase of energy from the grid. From the analysis of the design parameters, increasing the electrolyzer power and the size of the PV field reduces the L C O H , due to the economies of scale of both pieces of equipment. The optimization shows that it is possible to reach an L C O H for compressed hydrogen of 9.89 USD / kg for the centralized system and values of 5.88 USD / kg for the decentralized system.

title: Local optimization of CHP plant operation: an adaptively updated digital twin and linear programming
Comparative analysis of PV allocation rules in heterogeneous energy communities for collective self-consumption
abstract: This paper investigates how photovoltaic (PV) electricity allocation rules shape the technical, economic, and distributional performance of collective self-consumption schemes at both community and individual levels. A unified analytical framework is developed to compare four allocation mechanisms—static, hourly-variable, dynamic, and priority-based—across three community configurations: a prosumer-only community, an expanded community with fixed PV capacity, and an expanded community with PV capacity scaled to demand. The study is based on a real-case study of the CERCA energy community in Spain, using one year of measured hourly consumption, meteorological, and tariff data. Results show that allocation rules significantly influence both technical and economic outcomes. In the reference scenario, self-consumption ( SC ) rises from 0.39 to 0.41 (static, hourly-variable) to 0.45 (dynamic, priority), while IRR increases from 10.0% to 11.7% and payback decreases from 8.1 to 7.2 years. Community expansion with unchanged PV capacity improves local PV utilization, reaching SC values of 0.58–0.59, maximum IRR of 12.7% and payback of 6.7 years. At the individual level, priority allocation achieves the highest returns but the greatest dispersion of benefits (the coefficient of variation ( CV ) of individual SC is in the 20.7%–41.8% range), whereas dynamic allocation delivers comparable performance with a more balanced distribution ( CV of individual SC up to 9.2%). Sensitivity analysis shows that, for fixed PV capacity, profitability is maximized with 13–15 additional consumers, yielding an IRR of up to 13.3%. Overall, allocation rules are crucial in shaping both efficiency and equity in energy communities, with direct implications for policy and market design.

title: A probabilistic region-based model for evaluating the integrated hosting capacity of photovoltaics and electric vehicles in power distribution networks
A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

title: Flexibility-oriented hierarchical energy management for transmission–distribution–microgrid coordination
Data-Driven Electrolyte Design by Electrotopological State Descriptors for Na-Ion Batteries with Minimal Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Dissolution
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) determines the cycling reversibility of Na-ion batteries (NIBs). However, the high solubility of the Na-SEI continuously depletes the limited Na inventory in full cells, leading to accelerated electrolyte consumption and rapid capacity loss. To date, no general electrolyte design principles have been established to mitigate SEI dissolution, plaguing high Na-ion reversibility as an unsolved challenge. Herein, we quantitatively evaluate SEI dissolution across a broad range of NIB electrolytes and employ a closed-loop data-driven approach to correlate the dissolution behavior with over 200 electrolyte physicochemical descriptors. Among them, the solvent average electrotopological state (EState) index shows the strongest correlation with the SEI solubility. Guided by this insight, we designed high-EState electrolytes that suppressed SEI dissolution to only 6% of that in conventional electrolytes. The resulting minimal Na loss enabled a near-unity average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% over 1000 cycles in a hard carbon||NaMn0.33Fe0.33Ni0.33O2 full cell with all earth-abundant materials, successfully extending the End-of-Life battery model to Na-ion chemistry. This work elucidates quantitative correlations between electrolyte physicochemical properties and SEI dissolution, proposes EState-based electrolyte design principles with enhanced electrode–electrolyte interphase stability, and provides fundamental guidance to interphase designs for sustainable NIBs with high reversibility.

title: Data-driven distributionally robust planning of coastal distribution networks and PV-storage-EV stations for low-carbon energy transition
abstract: Coastal distribution networks (DNs) are becoming key infrastructure for the low-carbon energy transition as electric vehicle (EV) charging, photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage, and marine renewable procurement are increasingly coupled at the planning stage. Existing planning models, however, usually treat network expansion, PV-storage-EV station (PSES) deployment, low-carbon operation, and coastal asset degradation separately. This paper proposes a data-driven distributionally robust planning framework for coastal DNs and PSESs. The framework jointly optimizes radial network topology and PSES siting while incorporating salt-spray degradation costs, carbon-emission-flow (CEF)-based nodal carbon accounting, and tidal-generation-driven procurement costs. To represent heterogeneous uncertainty, the model combines continuous box uncertainty for load and PV availability with probability ambiguity over EV-charging scenarios generated from historical charging profiles. The resulting two-stage distributionally robust optimization problem is reformulated through exact relaxation of ESS mode binaries and KKT-based decomposition, and is solved by an inexact column-and-constraint generation (i-C&CG) algorithm. Case studies on a realistic 47-node coastal feeder show that salt-spray exposure can alter the selected topology and PSES siting, while the proposed planning scheme improves voltage quality, reduces annualized total cost, and reveals the cost--carbon trade-off of tidal procurement. The tailored i-C&CG algorithm obtains the same optimal design as conventional C&CG with about an order-of-magnitude reduction in solution time.

title: Spatial patterns of hybrid PV–CSP–TES configurations for green hydrogen production across Algeria
abstract: Existing studies have optimized hybrid PV–CSP plants or mapped suitable locations for solar hydrogen production, but the spatial dependence of the optimal hybrid architecture remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops a national-scale framework that couples GIS–FAHP screening with hourly PV–CSP–TES–electrolyzer simulation and site-specific NSGA-II optimization to determine how the cost-optimal system design changes across Algeria. At each meteorological location, PV capacity, CSP power-block capacity, TES duration, and solar multiple are jointly optimized for a fixed 50 MW electrolyzer, with the final configuration selected as the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) solution satisfying annual demand satisfaction (ADS) ≥ 90%. The resulting architecture varies substantially across the country: optimal PV capacity ranges from 70.03 to 168.86 MW, CSP power-block capacity from 50.00 to 92.98 MW, and solar multiple from 2.35 to 3.40, while annual hydrogen production remains comparatively stable at 7.58–7.65 kt H₂ yr −1 . Unconstrained LCOH ranges from 6.00 to 10.78 € kg −1 H₂ and narrows considerably after GIS-based deployment constraints are imposed. At Hassi R'Mel, the selected architecture combines approximately 100 MW PV, 50 MW CSP, SM = 2.80, and 16 h TES, achieving an LCOH of 6.53 € kg −1 H₂, 90.3% ADS and approximately 7.6 kt H₂ yr −1 . Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate and CSP capital cost as the strongest economic influences within the examined parameter ranges. A matched-output comparison shows that PV-only production can achieve lower LCOH when intermittency is acceptable, whereas PV–CSP–TES substantially increases electrolyzer utilization and production continuity. The results demonstrate that site-specific optimization is necessary to capture how economically preferred generation capacities and solar-field sizing adapt to local solar-resource conditions.

title: Bio-based deep eutectic solvents as advanced phase change media for solar thermal storage: Mechanisms, computational design, and industrial deployment challenges
From one cycle to full life: Ultra-early battery degradation assessment for operational assessment and rapid screening
Build for the future climate — or waste trillions of dollars
abstract: Development planning needs a permanent system that connects climate projections to the decisions that shape what infrastructure gets built.

title: TiO2/ZIF-8/CF-Based Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Intelligent Ammonia Sensing and Wireless Alarm in Livestock Farms
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ammonia, a common hazardous gas, severely endangers ecosystems and public health through unregulated industrial emissions and accidental leaks. Given the wide distribution and potential hazards of ammonia, a high-speed pulse airflow-powered triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) was constructed to realize ammonia sensing and environmental surveillance in animal breeding facilities. This device adopted a TiO2/ZIF-8/copper foam (CF) composite structure as the friction electrode (TZP-TENG). The composite nanogenerator efficiently harvested energy from high-pressure waste gas and exhibited outstanding electrical output performance. It delivered a short-circuit current output of 3.36 μA together with a peak power density reaching 41.19 μW at an NH3 concentration of 30 ppm. This device could illuminate 60 LEDs and supply different capacitors. For its excellent ammonia-sensing capability, the TZP-TENG could be integrated into a wireless early warning system to realize real-time monitoring and automatic alarming for high-concentration ammonia. Furthermore, the device is applicable to ammonia concentration detection in livestock farms, which helps stabilize the breeding environment and optimize the growth conditions of livestock and poultry. This design not only expands the technical approaches for ammonia detection but also enables intelligent regulation of breeding environments. It provides significant technical references and practical application demonstrations for harmful gas monitoring and environmental management in livestock breeding sites.

title: Photocatalytic control of diamond color center charge states via laser-induced surface oxidation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Color center spins in diamond nanostructures are a key resource for emerging quantum technologies. Their innate surface proximity makes precise control of diamond surface chemistry essential for optimizing their functionality and charge states. However, conventional surface functionalization methods provide limited control over the resulting surface termination and color-center charge state. Here, we demonstrate nonvolatile tuning of diamond’s surface termination through laser-induced oxidation of H-terminated diamond nanopillars. By tracking negatively charged silicon-vacancy (SiV−) photoluminescence as a charge-state proxy, we elucidate the carrier-assisted nature of this photocatalytic process through systematic photon-flux and photon-energy analyses, identifying defect charge cycling as a source of photogenerated carriers that drive the interfacial redox chemistry responsible for surface oxidation. Our results suggest that this approach may be applicable to other color centers and host materials for charge-state control and surface engineering in solid-state quantum devices.

title: Biomass-based platform for pesticide management balancing field efficacy with postharvest residue via dynamic adhesion switch
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recent nanopesticide formulations with strong adhesion enhance field efficacy by improving droplet retention on plant surfaces; however, their prolonged retention may increase postharvest residue risks, making it challenging to balance field performance with postharvest safety. Here we show a thermoresponsive adhesion switch inspired by biological adhesion mechanisms, employing lignin as a biomass-based platform to create a Pickering emulsion system (LgN-PE@EB) loaded with emamectin benzoate (EB). The system regulates its interfacial behavior with leaf surfaces through temperature-dependent phase transitions, achieving ~136% higher droplet retention than EB-EC under cultivation conditions and 114-275% increase in wash-off efficiency during postharvest cold-water washing. Additionally, lignin-derived UV shielding improves pesticide stability, while insecticidal activity (LC50) and biological safety (by crop fresh weight) increase by 64.9% and 61.1-165.9%, respectively. Overall, LgN-PE@EB provides a solution to address the spatiotemporal requirements of cultivation and postharvest, enhancing harvest flexibility and export safety for raw and high-value crops.

title: Internal Stress Effects on Electrode Stability in Coin Cells with Different Assembly Configurations
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Laboratory-level evaluation of electrode materials is typically conducted using hand-assembled coin cells (half cells) with a lithium metal counter electrode. However, the lack of standardized protocols for coin cell assembly across global laboratories results in inconsistent experimental outcomes, hindering data comparability and scientific progress in battery research. Herein, through fully automated robotic assembly of cells, we systematically investigated the influence of two different yet widely adopted cell configurations (spring and spacer located on the sides of the positive electrode cap and negative electrode cap are labeled as SS-P and SS-N, respectively) on the electrode materials. Different stress distributions were found on the electrodes due to the internal structural discrepancies, leading to variations in electrochemical performance, electrode structure, and electrode–electrolyte interphase properties. This work emphasizes the critical need to raise awareness about the standardization of battery assembly protocols, enabling researchers to fabricate coin cells with high repeatability and consistency.

title: Prestripping Protocol for Reconciling Lithium Dissolution and Galvanic Corrosion in Anode-Free Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The practical viability of high-energy-density anode-free lithium metal batteries is limited by the poor reversibility of lithium plating and stripping. Low-current stripping suppresses pitting and inactive Li formation but prolongs electrolyte exposure and galvanic corrosion, whereas high-current stripping shortens the corrosion time but promotes localized dissolution and structural disintegration. Here, we introduce a pre-stripping protocol consisting of a brief low-current stripping step followed immediately by higher-current bulk stripping, thereby establishing a uniform initial dissolution front while limiting the duration of Li–Cu galvanic coupling. Measurements across representative electrolyte formulations identify three factors associated with the balance between morphological regulation and corrosion loss: nascent solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) passivation, longer-term corrosion tolerance, and dynamic reaction area evolution. In strongly passivating formulations, the morphological benefit of prestripping outweighs the additional corrosion loss and improves Li reversibility. The protocol was further evaluated in 1 Ah anode-free pouch cells, supporting its applicability to practical cell configurations.

title: Marine volatile organic compounds air-sea exchange dynamics across a summer-to-autumn ecosystem transition
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Marine ecosystems influence atmospheric chemistry and climate by exchanging volatile organic compounds (VOCs) with the atmosphere, yet the chemical diversity and the environmental controls of the exchanged compounds remain poorly constrained. This gap persists because most marine observations are targeted, short-term, and narrow-suite measurements that seldom deliver chemically broad, continuous fluxes. Here we show that marine VOC exchange is chemically diverse and changes in magnitude and composition on event‑to‑season timescales. Using continuous flux measurements of 73 m/z features in the Baltic Sea, we observe a pronounced reorganization of net exchange: early organosulfur emissions diminish as cyanobacterial biomass declines (indicating water-side source limitation), while oxygenated and nitrogen-containing VOCs exhibit mixed behaviors ranging from deposition to episodic emissions (often dominated by wind-driven gas transfer kinetics). Together, these results demonstrate that chemically diverse marine VOC exchange is closely coupled to wind-induced mixing, water‑column structure, and phytoplankton community succession, highlighting the need to resolve these dynamic ecosystem states to predict future atmospheric composition.

title: A conceptual analysis of One Health and Person-Centred Practice
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Climate change, emerging infectious diseases and widening inequalities show that the health of people, animals and ecosystems cannot be separated. However, the ideas we use to understand this interdependence and those we use to organise and practise care have largely developed apart. Here we bring together One Health, linking human, animal and environmental health, and person-centred practice, focused on dignity, relationships and meaningful care. We show where they meet, where they clash and what each offers the other, arguing that care without responsibility for animals and ecosystems is incomplete, as is One Health without attention to lived experience.

title: Nationwide high-resolution assessment reveals the underestimated carbon sink of Chinese parks
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and promote carbon neutrality, parks, as Nature-based solutions, are often underestimated in their collective carbon sequestration function. Here we establish a high-resolution (30 -meter) carbon accounting framework for 8,137 parks across mainland China from 2010 to 2020, incorporating previously overlooked small parks. We show that parks constitute a substantial carbon sink. The total carbon sequestration based on Net Primary Productivity of parks nationwide reaches 52.7 million tonnes of carbon in 2020. Within the 5,425 urban parks, large parks exceeding 100 hectares (hm²) contribute over 90% of the total urban park sequestration, whereas parks of 10–50 hm2 drive the 2010–2020 shift from carbon sources to sinks. Medium and small sized parks show greater synergy between carbon sequestration and recreation services, informing locally tailored planning.

title: Bias-Free Photoelectrochemical Valorization of Glycerol at Both Photoelectrodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Harnessing photoelectrochemical systems to upgrade biomass-derived feedstocks such as glycerol offers a sustainable route for solar-driven chemical production. Nonetheless, glycerol conversion remains limited to the photoanode in current photoelectrochemical architectures, while the cathode predominantly generates hydrogen. Here, we propose a dual-electrode glycerol conversion strategy that enables simultaneous glycerol valorization at both photoelectrodes in a bias-free photoelectrochemical cell. This is achieved by enabling oxygen reduction at a CuBi2O4-based photocathode to generate H2O2, which is subsequently converted into reactive hydroxyl radicals, thereby driving photocathodic glycerol oxidation with glyceraldehyde as an important C3 product. In parallel, a Pt-decorated oxygen-deficient TiO2 photoanode promotes glycerol oxidation primarily via photogenerated holes. The coupled system operates without an externally applied bias, achieving a combined glyceraldehyde productivity of 32.1 μmol cm−2 h−1 based on the projected device area. This work establishes a dual-photoelectrode platform for solar-driven biomass valorization through distinct reaction pathways.

title: Longitudinal changes in mis-splicing in a cohort of female twins are widespread and highlight mechanisms of ageing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ageing is characterised by widespread cellular and molecular dysregulation including broad changes to gene expression. To study the impact of ageing on alternative splicing we profiled whole-blood RNA-seq data from 318 female twins (median age 61) at three time points over 6-8 years. We observe longitudinal changes across multiple classes of alternative splicing. Notably, intron retention, a marker of mis-splicing, shows a striking increase over time (P = 5.2 × 10−5). Twin modelling demonstrates that intron retention within an individual is heritable, with heritability increasing from 0.44 to 0.55 over time. Intron retention levels inversely associate with expression of RNA-binding proteins including SRSF4, ELAVL1, and AGO1, and show time-varying positive associations with diabetes status and markers of kidney disease, suggesting a link to chronic disease. Together, these findings suggest that mis-splicing is a heritable feature of human ageing which increases in prevalence over time and is associated with age-related disease.

title: A multimodal ultrasound foundation model for diagnosis of unexplained lymphadenopathy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Unexplained lymphadenopathy (ULA) leads to delayed diagnosis and increases the risk of disease progression due to the absence of specific clinical symptoms and indicative medical history during early stages, thereby increasing reliance on invasive biopsy. Existing ultrasound artificial intelligence approaches mainly use single-modality static images, limiting their generalizability and clinical applicability. Here, we develop and validate a multimodal model integrating B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging, ultrasound elastography, contrast-enhanced ultrasound videos, and clinical data for benign-malignant differentiation, etiologic stratification, and metastatic-origin prediction. This observational study includes both retrospective and prospective cohorts and uses a total of 154,740 multimodal keyframe images from 6,549 patients with pathologically confirmed lymphadenopathy across seven Chinese centers and 11 scanner manufacturers. The model shows robust performance across internal, external, device-heterogeneity, and reader study cohorts, outperforms senior radiologists across hierarchical tasks, and improves radiologists’ diagnostic performance across experience levels with model assistance, supporting its potential for noninvasive, efficient, and clinically aligned diagnosis of ULA.

title: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding how plants integrate developmental programs with temperature-responsive growth remains a central challenge in plant biology. Here, we uncover a mechanism by which a canonical leaf senescence regulator directly governs thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis. We show that ORESARA1 (ORE1), best known for orchestrating leaf senescence, promotes warm temperature-induced hypocotyl and petiole elongation and the expression of warmth-responsive genes IAA19 and YUC8. Mechanistically, ORE1 acts upstream of PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 4 (PIF4), the central transcriptional hub for thermomorphogenesis. ORE1 does not alter PIF4 transcript abundance but specifically stabilizes PIF4 protein under warmth by physically interacting with PIF4 in the nucleus to enhance its deubiquitination. We identify the deubiquitinase UBP12/UBP13 as an essential component of this pathway; however, PIF4 does not bind UBP12/UBP13 directly. Biochemical and genetic analyses demonstrate that ORE1 functions as a molecular scaffold, recruiting PIF4 to an ORE1-UBP12/UBP13 complex to position UBP12/UBP13 for PIF4 deubiquitination. This UBP12/UBP13-ORE1-PIF4 module establishes a paradigm where a senescence factor regulates thermomorphogenesis by orchestrating deubiquitinase-mediated tuning of PIF4 proteostasis.

title: Eco-evolutionary dynamics of active virus-host interactions in a freshwater lake revealed through metaHi-C
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Detecting active phage–bacteria interactions in natural microbial communities remains a major limitation for understanding their ecological dynamics and associated co-evolutionary processes. Here, we apply metaHi-C, a chromosome conformation capture method, to resolve active virus–host associations in a freshwater microbial community. From >900 microbial and >33,000 viral Hi-C–assembled genomes, we identify 100 high-confidence phage–host linkages spanning major freshwater bacterial lineages, including Limnohabitans, Acidimicrobium, Synechococcus, Candidatus Nanopelagicus, Candidatus Planktophila, Candidatus Methylopumilus, and Polynucleobacter. The inferred networks reveal signatures consistent with diverse infection patterns, including broad-host-range phages, cellular-level co-infection, kill-the-winner-like dynamics, and one-to-one interactions. These ecological patterns are associated with signatures of diversifying selection in host-interaction genes, consistent with host-range expansion, alongside conserved genomic regions in broad-host-range and co-infecting phages, indicating functional constraints on essential infection modules. Together, these results demonstrate that metaHi-C enables the direct detection of active phage–host associations within a community snapshot, and that, when combined with longitudinal metagenomic recruitment analyses, this approach can link community-level infection dynamics to underlying evolutionary processes, revealing how these forces shape population dynamics of freshwater bacteria.

title: Harnessing plant cells as oral drug delivery capsules for synergistic therapy of ulcerative colitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cell-derived carriers are important excipients in drug delivery systems; however, most studies have focused on mammalian cells. Plant cells, by comparison, offer intrinsic therapeutic potential and feature a bilayer structure composed of cell wall and cell membrane. Here, we utilize the carrot plant cells as oral colon-targeting drug delivery vehicles leveraging their intrinsic therapeutic properties and the outer layer of cell wall. Utilizing ulcerative colitis and glucocorticoid budesonide as a disease and drug model, the drug loading strategy, colon microenvironment sensitivity, colon-specific drug release and anti-inflammation efficacies of the plant cell-based delivery system are evaluated. In particular, the budesonide-loaded liposomes are linked to carrot cells via click chemistry to achieve budesonide-loaded carrot cells, which are validated to maintain stable and decrease the drug distribution and absorption in stomach and small intestine, while disintegrated by local microbiota after reaching colon to allow colon-targeting release. The glucocorticoid drug, intrinsic anti-inflammation substances in plant cells and the short-chain fatty acids generated by cell wall enzymatic degradation work synergistically to strengthen the therapeutic efficacy in ulcerative colitis mice models. This work provides insights into the development of plant-based drug excipients and offers an alternative strategy for the targeted treatment of colonic diseases.

title: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: CARM1 is an arginine methyltransferase with a well-established role in regulating gene expression, but its cytoplasmic functions remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we identified ALIX, a cytoplasmic protein acting with the ESCRT-III machinery in numerous membrane remodeling events, as a partner and substrate of CARM1. We demonstrate that CARM1 methylates arginine residues within the proline-rich motif of ALIX. At the molecular level, ALIX methylation impairs SH3-dependent association with CD2AP, CIN85, and endophilin-A2 that are required for cytokinesis. Using a mutant of ALIX that is unable to bind these proteins, we further show that these interactions are essential for ALIX functions during cytokinesis. Mechanistically, ALIX methylation controls the levels of CD2AP at the cytokinetic midbody, which are known to be critical for successful cytokinesis. Altogether, this work highlights the significance of arginine methylation as a regulatory post-translational modification important for the final step of cell division, by modulating interactions between proline-rich domains and their SH3-containing partners.

title: Prioritizing the next decade of research in bat infectious disease (batID)
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bats are widely studied as asymptomatic hosts of viruses that cause high case fatality rates in humans. Though prior research into bat infections has been traditionally virus-focused, there is growing interest to more holistically understand bat-microbe relationships. In July 2025 the fourth International Symposium on the Infectious Diseases of Bats (‘BatID 2025’) convened, synthesizing the current state of bat-microbe research from within-host to population-level processes. Here, we outline five questions that emerged from this meeting as priority future directions. We share this review with the aim of stimulating future research, emphasizing the need for data sharing and interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Immunoglobulin A promotes stable colonization of Bifidobacterium to protect against allergic inflammation under fiber deprivation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Modern dietary patterns, particularly those low in fermentable fiber, are associated with intestinal dysbiosis and increased susceptibility to allergic disease, yet individuals exposed to similar diets often display markedly different outcomes. This variability suggests that protective commensal microbes may persist in some hosts, but the mechanisms that maintain these bacteria and enable their immunoregulatory effects remain unclear. Here, we show that Bifidobacterium induces self-recognizing, T cell–dependent immunoglobulin A (IgA) that enhances its mucosal adhesion and persistence under fiber-deprived conditions. Loss of this IgA response reduces Bifidobacterium colonization and increases allergic inflammation. We further demonstrate that Bifidobacterium-derived metabolites, including genistein and indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), suppress mast cell (MC) activation and T helper 2 (Th2) responses through distinct mechanisms, attenuating allergic inflammation and systemic anaphylaxis in vivo. Together, these findings reveal a self-reinforcing host–microbial mutualism in which adaptive IgA preserves, rather than eliminates, beneficial commensals to maintain immune homeostasis.

title: A leptin receptor–LRP1 complex in the choroid plexus and tanycytes mediates leptin entry into the mouse brain
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Obesity is characterized by central leptin resistance, in which elevated circulating leptin fails to reach or activate its hypothalamic targets. Yet the mechanisms that mediate leptin transport into the brain remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that in the choroid plexus (ChP), leptin promotes the physical coupling of the leptin receptor (LepR) and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein-1 (LRP1) to form a functional LRP1–LepR complex. Deletion of LepR or LRP1 in Foxj1-expressing cells, which include ChP epithelial cells and hypothalamic tanycytes, disrupts leptin entry into the brain, impairs hypothalamic leptin signaling, and induces hyperphagia and obesity. Intracerebroventricular leptin restores the anorexigenic response, confirming that the defect is in transport rather than central signaling. In diet-induced obese mice, formation of the LRP1–LepR complex is impaired, contributing to leptin resistance. These findings identify the LRP1–LepR complex in the ChP and tanycytes as an essential gateway for leptin entry into the brain and a potential therapeutic target in obesity.

title: A scalable pipeline for patient-matched pediatric solid tumor models and cell lines
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Most pediatric solid tumor cell lines were established decades ago, and patient-matched organoids and xenografts are rarely available, limiting their translational utility. We present an approach to generate triads of patient-matched xenografts, three-dimensional organoids, and two-dimensional primary cultures from pediatric tumors, including rhabdomyosarcoma, osteosarcoma, neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma, Wilms tumor, and retinoblastoma. We have generated organoids from 135 pediatric tumors, alongside 82 patient-matched two-dimensional primary cultures and 20 new cell lines. When orthotopically implanted into immunocompromised mice, these models preserved the molecular and cellular features of the original patient tumor. We completed 365 single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing experiments encompassing over 2.2 million cells to evaluate cellular heterogeneity across triads. All samples are renewable, and over 3000 vials have been cryopreserved for unrestricted distribution through the Childhood Solid Tumor Network. In this work, we present a comprehensive methodological toolbox for generating patient-matched triads for advancing preclinical pediatric cancer research.

title: ALKR1275Q expands Schwann cell precursor-like cells during sympathoadrenal commitment, creating a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) arises from neural crest-derived cells of the sympathoadrenal lineage, yet how predisposing genetic lesions influence early human development remains poorly understood. Here, we use patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models carrying the familial ALK R1275Q mutation to investigate its role during sympathoadrenal differentiation. We show that ALK R1275Q delays lineage maturation and sustains a proliferative progenitor state characterized by elevated ALK signaling and expansion of a Schwann cell precursor (SCP)-like population. This SCP-like state persists during differentiation and is reduced by ALK inhibition or CRISPR-based mutation correction. Although ALK R1275Q alone is insufficient to drive tumor formation in vivo, it enhances susceptibility to oncogenic transformation in cooperation with MYCN. Together, these findings support a model in which ALK R1275Q reshapes developmental trajectories by maintaining a proliferative SCP-like progenitor state, thereby creating a permissive cellular context for NB initiation.

title: Spatiotemporal brain dynamics of limb ownership perception
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We experience our limbs as our own, but how does the brain generate this fundamental sense of body ownership? Previous studies have relied mainly on fMRI or lesion mapping, providing a static view of the neural mechanisms underlying body ownership. Using magnetoencephalography, robotically controlled visuotactile stimulation, and multivariate analysis across the rubber hand illusion, a real hand condition, and multiple control conditions, we identified source vector dissimilarity patterns reflecting ownership of the left arm. Three phases of ownership-specific activity patterns emerged: (i) anticipatory patterns in medial frontal cortex, right posterior parietal cortex, and right posterior cerebellum before tactile stimulation; (ii) multisensory integration patterns in right dorsal and ventral premotor cortex, right posterior parietal cortex, and anterior cerebellum at 116–156 ms poststimulus; and (iii) later bilateral insular and left hemisphere patterns at 184–232 ms. These findings provide a whole-brain, time-resolved map of activity patterns underlying body ownership, revealing its dynamic neural construction.

title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. This method was built upon the design of an ultralow-volume, shallow 96-well plate for robust rapid collection and processing of single voxels. Using a commonly accessible MS platform, USMCP-MS enables reproducible label-free quantification of ~1,700 and ~2,500 protein groups from single voxels of fresh frozen mouse brain tissue at 20 µm × 20 µm × 10 µm ( ~ 1 cell region) and 50 µm × 50 µm × 10 µm ( ~ 6 cell region), respectively. More importantly, USMCP-MS can be broadly applied to different types of tissues (fresh frozen, OCT-embedded, and FFPE) for 2D proteome mapping of region areas of interest at 50–100 µm spatial resolutions, revealing spatially resolved protein signatures and region-specific signaling pathways. With its further improvement, USMCP-MS may pave the way for routine, robust, scalable proteome mapping of tissues at single-cell spatial resolution.

title: Dipolar Heterointerface Enabled by Molecular Zwitterionicity for Rigid and Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Poor interfacial compatibility at the interface between the electron transport layer (ETL) and the perovskite gives rise to defect-rich interfaces with weak adhesion, representing a major critical limitation that hinders the efficiency, operational stability, and mechanical robustness of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Herein, a zwitterionic molecule, 3-(1-pyridinio)-1-propanesulfonate (Pyps), is introduced at the ETL/perovskite interface to construct a dipolar heterointerface, where the sulfonate (–SO3–) and pyridinium moieties synergistically reinforce interfacial bonding, passivate buried interfacial defects, and enhance the conductivity of the SnO2 ETL, while its large intrinsic dipole moment tailors the interfacial energy-level alignment to both improve charge extraction and suppress recombination. As a result, the dipolar heterointerface enables champion efficiencies of 26.86% and 25.50% for rigid and flexible PSCs, respectively. The unencapsulated PSCs retain over 93.2% of their initial performance under continuous operation after 1300 h, demonstrating the promise of dipolar heterointerface engineering for high-performance PSCs.

Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
abstract: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. We implement this principle through an axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion direct laser writing strategy that keeps the depletion zone aligned with the Gaussian excitation focus. Axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion produces isolated lines 56.2 nm wide and resolves gratings with a 150-nm period and a 110-nm linewidth at a 160 μm depth with a numerical aperture of 1.27, while maintaining a 167.3-nm linewidth at 1,400 μm, using a numerical aperture of 1.1. We use axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion to fabricate axially extended mesoscopic optical systems, including 4f systems, vortex phase plates, miniaturized objectives and microlens arrays.

title: Single-Atom Catalysts for Biomass Valorization
abstract: Abstract Biomass, the only renewable organic carbon resource on Earth, offers a promising feedstock for producing value-added chemicals and fuels. However, the principal challenge in biomass valorization stems from the inherent complexity of its functional groups, necessitating catalysts capable of precisely activating specific C–O/C═O/C═C bonds while suppressing undesired side reactions. Single-atom catalysts (SACs), featuring unique geometric and electronic structures as well as high atomic utilization efficiency, have shown potential for highly effective biomass conversion in thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. Drawing upon recent continuous efforts on SACs in biomass valorization, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances in applying SACs to the transformation of main components of lignocellulosic biomass and their platform molecules. Structure–activity relationships and catalytic behavior of SACs under different external stimuli (e.g., thermal, electrical, and photonic) are emphasized, showcasing their innovative applications. The important factors governing catalytic activity and selectivity with a particular focus on the geometric and electronic structures of active sites are discussed, aiming to derive fundamental principles for the rational design of efficient and selective catalysts for biomass valorization. Finally, an outlook highlights the key challenges and prospects in this flourishing field.

title: Quasi-degenerate cation occupation enables oxygen-vacancy defect healing in nonlinear optical crystals
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which couple with dopants and obscure or degrade the intrinsic properties. Therefore, chemical substitution that enables atomically precise engineering of materials without generating defect structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to overcome this detrimental coupling and successfully apply it to the langasite-family nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal, La3TiGa5O14 (LGTi). Therein, the cross-site occupation of Ti and Ti3+/Ti4+ redox flexibility improves the kinetic accessibility of oxygen-vacancy (VO) defects associated with cation disorder, enabling their removal during oxidative annealing. The oxidized LGTi single crystal has a VO-related defect concentration below the electron paramagnetic resonance detection limit, with a laser damage threshold of 2.53 GW/cm2 and a large NLO coefficient of 3.51 pm/V, both exceeding the previously reported values for bulk langasite-family crystals. Overall, this work provides a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to mitigate substitution-induced defects in structurally complex crystalline systems and has great prospects in enhancing material performance.

title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Mediated Uptake and Delivery of Indocyanine Green/Doxorubicin-Loaded Stimuli-Responsive Dendrimers to Tumors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Systemic administration of nanocarriers can be limited by rapid clearance and off-target distribution, motivating the investigation of cell-based carrier strategies. Here, we evaluated skin-derived mesenchymal stem cells (S-MSCs) as carriers for PEGylated poly(amidoamine) dendrimer nanoclusters (DNCs) co-loaded with the chemotherapeutic doxorubicin (DOX) and the photothermal dye indocyanine green (ICG). The dendrimer nanoclusters (DNCs-ICG-DOX-PEG) enabled effective co-encapsulation of both cargoes and retained the optical properties required for NIR activation. Confocal imaging confirmed intracellular retention of DOX-associated fluorescence, predominantly within vesicular compartments, for up to 48 h after DNC loading, whereas free DOX was largely lost from S-MSCs within 24 h. At lower tested concentrations, DNC-loading preserved S-MSC metabolic activity, surface marker expression, and migratory function. Irradiation at 808 nm increased DOX release from the DNC formulations and produced an irradiation-dependent reduction in S-MSC metabolic activity. In a pilot murine LLC1 tumor model, S-MSCs preloaded with DNCs and administered adjacent to the tumor were detected within tumor tissue after 24 h, indicating that DNC loading did not abolish local tumor-directed migration. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of using S-MSCs as carriers for NIR-responsive, DOX- and ICG-loaded dendrimer nanoclusters and provide a foundation for further studies of cargo biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy.

title: Non Hermitian synthetic phase shifter with topologically protected phase control via tunable losses
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Phase shifters are fundamental reconfigurable components in photonic circuits. In conjunction with passive elements, they control light flow and serve as foundational building blocks for diverse applications, including communication, sensing, analog signal processing, and quantum control. Conventional phase shifters achieve phase control by modulating the refractive index through various physical mechanisms such as thermo-optic or electro-optic effects. However, despite expectations that such index–based approaches would integrate seamlessly, they, in practice, restrict circuit size, bandwidth, and scalability and thus become bottlenecks to large–scale photonic integration. Here, we introduce an alternative phase–control approach based on optical loss modulation. We demonstrate a synthetic phase shifter that uses two independently controlled loss–modulation stages combined with multipath interference to achieve full–cycle phase tunability while maintaining constant amplitude. We develop a theoretical framework based on conserved topological charges to show how synthetic phase control can be achieved via non-Hermitian effects, enabling robust, topologically protected phase control. By shifting the paradigm from index control to loss modulation, the proposed synthetic phase shifter could pave the way for scalable integrated photonic systems that support applications from communications and sensing to photonic classical and quantum information processing.

title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO2/H2O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. This work offers a route toward self-correcting scientific databases and toward database curation driven by large language models.

title: Targeted Gene Delivery with Enhanced Efficacy through Heterochiral Coassembly of Peptides
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of gene-based therapeutics faces substantial delivery challenges. To address this, we report a strategy involving heterochiral peptide coassembly to create an efficient peptidyl delivery platform. Our experimental results reveal that equimolar mixture of l-KH-CCR and d-KH-CCR peptides exhibit significantly enhanced gene condensation efficiency, improved structural stability, and more effective endosomal membrane disruption compared to their pure enantiomeric counterparts. These superior properties facilitate increased cellular internalization and efficient endosomal escape, ultimately leading to optimized delivery of various gene therapeutics, particularly mRNA and siRNA. Building upon these findings, we engineered a four-component system that integrates a targeting peptide and PEG-conjugated anti-adhesion peptides within the heterochiral peptide system, which was evaluated for pulmonary mRNA delivery and expression in an orthotopic A549 lung tumor model. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that these peptides can effectively bind to mRNA through a combination of electrostatic, hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, leading to the self-assembly of nanoparticles with accessible targeting and anti-adhesion motifs. In this model, the targeting-peptide-containing heterochiral formulation produced higher lung reporter expression than the corresponding homochiral formulations. These findings underscore the pivotal influence of chirality in optimizing the performance of peptidyl nanocarriers for targeted gene delivery applications.

title: Magnetic Field Gradients Break Transport Symmetry, Enabling the Separation of Thermodynamically Similar Critical Metals
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Field-programmed control of interfacial ion transport offers a route to tune electrodeposit composition and electrochemical selectivity in complex feeds, where chemically similar ions often co-deposit because small thermodynamic differences are overwhelmed by coupled transport and reaction. Here, we establish magneto-electrochemical reactive separation as a strategy for controlling competitive ion supply and electrodeposition through magnetic-field geometry. Operando Mach–Zehnder interferometry directly resolves magnetic-field-induced concentration redistribution near the electrode under open-circuit and reactive conditions. Under the open circuit, cobalt (Co)- and nickel (Ni)-containing electrolytes exhibit distinct concentration responses, demonstrating that magnetic perturbation preconditions the interfacial ion inventory before charge transfer. Under cathodic polarization, the response reflects competition between field-coupled resupply and reaction-driven depletion. Although Co exhibits the stronger open-circuit magnetic response, Ni shows the larger deposition enhancement because the selected potential places Ni in a more strongly transport-limited regime, while Co remains under mixed transport/kinetic control. A reduced transport model provides a consistent framework for interpreting this coupling among interfacial accumulation, depletion, and reaction kinetics. In mixed Co/Ni electrolytes, magnetic geometry increases Co/Ni selectivity from 8.5 to 28.5 for a 1Co:9Ni feed, whereas an alternative geometry produces a deposit containing 80.8 wt % Ni from the same electrolyte. Extending this principle to an olivine-derived leachate containing 41 ppm Ni and 411 ppm Fe, a diametrically magnetized configuration increases Ni/Fe selectivity from 0.45 to 12.42, despite an approximately 1:10 Ni/Fe concentration ratio in the feed. These results establish magnetic geometry as a tunable control variable for restructuring interfacial transport under direct mixed-ion competition and enabling field-programmable elemental separation from complex electrolytes.

title: Heparin-Decorated Hydrogel Microspheres Enable Bioactive Islet Encapsulation and Sustained Glycemic Control in Diabetic Mice
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is characterized by immune-mediated β-cell destruction and chronic insulin deficiency. Pancreatic islet transplantation offers a promising approach to restore endogenous insulin production; however, the early post-transplantation period remains a critical barrier to successful graft function, as rapid protein adsorption, coagulation activation, and inflammatory cell recruitment at the material interface can compromise encapsulated islet viability. Here, we develop heparin-decorated hydrogel microcapsules to regulate early material–host interactions and improve the performance of islet encapsulation. Heparin was incorporated into a poly-l-lysine-modified gelatin (PLL–GEL) network through electrostatic complexation, where PLL was covalently anchored onto gelatin via transglutaminase-mediated cross-linking, and subsequently integrated with sodium alginate microcapsules fabricated by electrospraying and calcium-mediated ionic gelation. The resulting microcapsules exhibited uniform morphology, structural stability, and favorable physicochemical properties. Heparin incorporation reduced fibrinogen adsorption, prolonged coagulation times, and decreased macrophage adhesion, indicating improved early hemocompatibility and reduced material-induced cellular interactions. Furthermore, macrophages exposed to heparin-containing microcapsules showed altered immune-related transcriptional responses, suggesting regulation of early host responses. Encapsulated islets maintained high viability and glucose-responsive insulin secretion in vitro. Following intraperitoneal transplantation into diabetic mice, heparin-decorated microcapsules improved graft retention and sustained glycemic control over 30 days. Collectively, this study presents a functional material strategy for optimizing the early-stage compatibility of hydrogel microcapsules in islet transplantation.

title: Defect Passivation and Electric Field Homogenization at the Buried SnO2/Perovskite Interface via SIP-Na Modification
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The nonideality of the buried SnO2/perovskite interface is a key bottleneck restricting the performance of perovskite solar cells. However, there is still a lack of in-depth understanding of the morphological characteristics and physical mechanisms of this interface. This study systematically investigated the multifunctional optimization effect of sodium 5-sulfoisophthalic acid (SIP-Na) as an interface modifier between SnO2 and perovskite. With the help of mechanical interface exposure technology, intuitive evidence has been provided for the control manipulation of buried interfaces. The scanning electron microscopy results show that SIP-Na can effectively eliminate interface voids and guide the formation of high-quality crystals with larger grain size and lower stress in the perovskite. In addition, COMSOL simulation analysis reveals that SIP-Na treatment can significantly homogenize the interface electric field distribution. Under the joint promotion of the multiple optimization mechanisms mentioned above, the final device achieved a champion efficiency of 25.36% and a high open-circuit voltage of 1.265 V. This study combines direct interface characterization and physical simulation to deeply reveal the synergistic enhancement mechanism of molecular modifiers at the buried interface, providing a new perspective and theoretical support for interface engineering research.

title: Interfacial redox mediation enables efficient, stable wide-bandgap perovskites for perovskite-organic tandem solar cells
abstract: A reactive co-adsorption strategy couples 4-carboxybenzenethiol with hole-selective molecules (HSMs) to build a redox-active buried interface in wide-bandgap perovskites. Redox shuttling converts I2 and Pb0 back to halides, suppressing ion-migration-driven phase segregation. The 1.79 eV sub-cell reaches PCE of 21.02% (VOC for 1.375 V) and shows T90 over 800 h at 65°C MPPT, enabling 27.5% monolithic perovskite-organic tandems.

title: Mechanically Robust CaCO3/Alginate Double-Walled Capsules for Sustained Soil Hydrophobicity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This study presents a double-walled capsule designed for sustained release to restore hydrophobicity in soils and to mitigate water infiltration in ground infrastructure. The capsule consists of an inner calcium alginate shell encapsulating a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) core and an outer shell of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) formed via microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP). Comprehensive characterization reveals that the MICP-derived CaCO3 shell significantly enhances the mechanical properties of the capsule: nanoindentation shows a 15-fold increase in Young’s modulus (6.58 GPa) and a 7-fold increase in hardness (0.280 GPa) compared to single-walled calcium alginate capsules. Thermal stability is also improved, with a higher residual mass (41.4 vs 8.6%) at 800 °C. Release studies evaluating different core loadings (20 and 40%) in sand under saturated and humid conditions demonstrate that the double-walled architecture significantly reduces and controls PDMS release relative to alginate-only capsules. While single-walled capsules suffered from premature leakage in humid conditions due to evaporation-induced shrinkage, the CaCO3 shell effectively resisted structural shrinkage, ensuring a sustained cumulative release. Release kinetic analysis using the Korsmeyer-Peppas model further corroborated this physical barrier effect: the release exponent (n) was significantly reduced from the non-Fickian regime (0.577–0.652) for single-walled capsules down to the Fickian diffusion-dominated regime (0.369–0.470) for double-walled capsules. This fabrication strategy yields robust capsules that enable controlled, long-term functional regeneration, offering a promising pathway toward self-healing soils.

title: Ligand-Engineered Metal–Organic Framework Nanoparticles Link Phase-Selective Localization to Interfacial Reinforcement in Immiscible Polymer Blends
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermodynamic immiscibility and insufficient interfacial adhesion limit the mechanical performance of polymer blends. Although nanoparticles can modify polymer–polymer interfaces, how ligand-dependent surface characteristics relate to phase-selective localization and the accompanying mechanical response remains incompletely understood. Here, a series of ligand-engineered UiO-66 nanoparticles was introduced into polypropylene/polystyrene (PP/PS) blends to compare localization within the PP matrix, the PS dispersed phase, and the PP/PS interfacial region. In the PP/PS blend containing TCPE@UiO-66-NH2/CF3 nanoparticles prepared from an equimolar linker feed, fluorescence is concentrated near the PP/PS interfaces. This blend exhibits pronounced PS-domain refinement and the largest increase in tensile toughness among the formulations examined. At a nanoparticle loading of 1.0 wt %, the tensile toughness increases from 6.6 to 65.5 J cm–3, accompanied by increases in tensile strength and elongation at break. Dual-channel confocal microscopy using MOF-confined and phase-selective aggregation-induced emission probes shows that nanoparticle fluorescence remains associated with PS-rich regions during early tensile loading and that elongated fluorescence features appear during necking. Compared with uncompatibilized PP/PS, the mixed-linker blend shows less pronounced interfacial separation and more extensive drawing of the PP matrix in scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images. Generic coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) models yield localization trends qualitatively consistent with the microscopy observations and indicate improved stress transfer when hybrid particles localize at the interface. Together, these results correlate ligand-dependent nanoparticle localization with coupled changes in phase morphology, interfacial response, and tensile toughness.

title: Threading the Pearl Necklace like Gel Skeleton with Sub-Nanometer Scale String for Structural Toughening of Composite SiO2 Aerogels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional inorganic oxide aerogels suffer from high brittleness due to their discontinuous “stringless pearl necklace” microstructure, which limits their industrial application despite superior insulating properties. Conventional fiber or polymer reinforcement often compromises thermal performance or fails owing to scale mismatch. To address this challenge, herein, a “continuous backbone directed growth” strategy was developed, utilizing phloretic acid (PA) to modify GdOOH sub-1 nm nanowires (SNWs) for the in situ growth of silica nanoparticles. This “beads-on-string” architecture spatially optimizes the distribution of the silica phase, preventing random aggregation and ensuring a highly uniform porous structure. Simultaneously, the SNWs act as sub-nanoscale threads that strongly reinforce the skeletal junctions. The resulting silica-sub-1 nm nanowire aerogel (SSA) composite accommodates substantial compressive deformation without macroscopic fracture and exhibits a low room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.0262 W m–1 K–1. During thermogravimetric analysis, SSA retained 76% of its initial mass upon heating to 800 °C. Separate tests demonstrated its thermal insulation performance at temperatures ranging from –30 to 150 °C. This study provides a new paradigm for sub-nanoscale reinforcement that successfully decouples mechanical integrity from functional porosity for next-generation thermal protection.

title: In Situ Growth and High Performance of Tightly Coupled Lead-Free Perovskite-Based Type-II Heterojunctions for CO2 Reduction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rational construction of environmentally friendly heterojunctions with a type-II band alignment is an effective strategy for reducing photogenerated charge recombination and enhancing photocatalytic activity, whereas the carrier migration efficiency strongly depends on the interfacial contact quality. Herein, a lead-free perovskite-based heterojunction, Bi2O3/Cs3Bi2Br9 (BO/CBB), is synthesized through the in situ growth of Cs3Bi2Br9 (CBB) particles on Bi2O3 (BO) flakes. The optimized BO/CBB sample exhibits the highest CO production rate of 42.3 μmol g–1 h–1 among the compared photocatalysts, which is 3.2 and 10.8 times higher than those of pristine BO and CBB, respectively. Notably, the CO yield of in situ-grown BO/CBB is 7.4 times higher than that of the electrostatically self-assembled sample, highlighting the advantage of the in situ growth strategy. Experimental results and first-principles calculations reveal that the tightly coupled interface facilitates interfacial charge migration, enabling efficient type-II charge transfer and thereby promoting the spatial separation of photogenerated electron–hole pairs. Analysis of the reaction intermediates indicates that BO/CBB effectively reduces the reaction energy barriers of the first two elementary steps in CO2 reduction. This work provides a feasible strategy for constructing high-quality type-II lead-free perovskite heterojunctions for efficient photocatalytic CO2 reduction.

title: Polyimide-Encapsulated Ag/Aramid-Reinforced Graphene Aerogel for Ultrasensitive and Fatigue-Resistant Wearable Motion Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Graphene aerogel (GA) combines ultralow density, high porosity, excellent conductivity, and mechanical tunability, making it ideal for piezoresistive sensing. However, achieving both high sensitivity and robust mechanical performance remains challenging. Herein, we report a flexible pressure sensor based on a hierarchical PI/Ag@AFs/GA composite: polyimide (PI) fibers reinforce the GA scaffold, preserving porosity while enhancing structural integrity; silver-coated aramid fibers (Ag@AFs) are interwoven into the GA network, forming a percolating conductive pathway that lowers electron transport resistance. The resulting sensor delivers high sensitivity (7.63 kPa–1), rapid response/recovery (385/386 ms), and exceptional compressive strength (153 kPa at 90% strain). It enables reliable human motion monitoring and tactile signal transmission, underscoring its potential for applications in electronic skin, wearable health electronics, and soft robotics.

title: Porphyrin-Phenothiazine-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enhanced Photocatalytic Nitrogen Fixation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven photocatalytic nitrogen reduction represents a promising and environmentally benign approach for ammonia synthesis. However, developing efficient photocatalysts capable of converting nitrogen to ammonia under ambient conditions remains a significant challenge. Porphyrin compounds exhibit excellent photosensitive properties with strong absorption across both the ultraviolet and visible regions of the solar spectrum, while phenothiazine offers unique optoelectronic activity. In this study, we integrated these two motifs and synthesized a series of novel metal-free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) by structural modification of the phenothiazine linker with a methyl group and with oxygen-containing functional groups. All three frameworks are active for N2 photoreduction under visible light, and the activity depends systematically on the linker: the sulfone-functionalized COF-3 reaches 109.6 ± 3.6 μmol g–1 h–1 (1866.2 ± 60.7 μg h–1 gcat–1), outperforming both the unmodified (COF-1) and the methyl-modified (COF-2) frameworks. Mechanistic analysis and theoretical calculations revealed that the introduced oxygen atoms facilitate the separation and transport of photogenerated electrons within the framework. This work shows that rational molecular-level pre-design and fine-tuning of the linker can profoundly influence the structural and optoelectronic properties of COF-based photocatalysts, enabling superior activity without the need for metallic elements or co-catalysts.

title: Interfacial Stabilization of Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries via Steric-Hindrance-Induced Li+ Coordination Regulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Strong Li–O coordination and labile α-hydrogens in ether-based polymer electrolytes are key contributors to sluggish ion transport and electrode interfacial degradation in solid-state lithium metal batteries. Here, we propose a steric-hindrance-regulated molecular design that simultaneously considers polymer-chain coordination and interfacial chemistry by introducing methyl-substituted bulky side chains into the polymer backbone (P-BnMA). The side-chain architecture sterically regulates the accessibility of polymer coordination sites while eliminating reactive α-hydrogens, thereby driving anions into the primary Li+ coordination shell without severely restricting polymer segmental mobility. The resultant anion-rich coordination microenvironment promotes the formation of inorganic-rich interfaces (LiF, Li3N, and Li2O) on both electrodes, ensuring interfacial stability during prolonged cycling. Accordingly, Li|P-BnMA|Li symmetric cells operate stably for over 4000 h. LFP|P-BnMA|Li cells retain 80.4% capacity after 1000 cycles, and Ni-rich NCM90|P-BnMA|Li cells retain 82.0% capacity after 100 cycles at 4.3 V. Such a side-chain engineering strategy couples Li+ coordination regulation with interfacial stabilization, providing a practical approach for the molecular design of polymer electrolytes.

title: pH-Responsive Polymer-Brush Engineering Enables Photothermal Amplification of Evodiamine-Associated Ferroptotic Responses
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ferroptosis offers an alternative therapeutic strategy for tumors resistant to apoptosis, but its efficacy is often limited by inefficient drug delivery and cellular antioxidant defenses. Here, we develop a pH-responsive, photothermally activatable nanoplatform (EVO@PDA@PDMAEMA, EPP) that integrates adaptive evodiamine (EVO) delivery with photothermal amplification of ferroptosis-associated responses. The PDMAEMA polymer-brush interface enables pH-dependent charge regulation and enhanced EVO release under mildly acidic conditions. Meanwhile, the PDA core provides stable 808 nm photothermal conversion with an efficiency of 58.52%. EPP enhanced cellular uptake and tumor-associated accumulation, while near-infrared (NIR) irradiation further increased its cytotoxicity and ferroptosis-associated responses, including iron accumulation, glutathione depletion, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, lipid oxidative damage, and suppression of the SLC7A11/GPX4 axis. Ferrostatin-1 rescue supported a substantial contribution of ferroptosis to EPP-mediated cell death. In tumor-bearing mice, EPP + NIR achieved an additional 50.95% reduction in tumor volume relative to EPP alone, accompanied by consistent ferroptosis-associated responses and without evident systemic toxicity under the tested conditions. These findings demonstrate a polymer-brush-based strategy that couples pH-responsive drug delivery with photothermal stimulation to enhance EVO-associated ferroptotic activity and antitumor efficacy.
