title: Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
abstract:
Abstract
                  Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management.

title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
abstract: Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantio‐ and Regioselective Addition of Silicon and Boron Nucleophiles to Methylene Cyclobutene for the Construction of Quaternary Stereocenters
abstract: ABSTRACT A nickel‐catalyzed enantio‐ and regioselective addition of silicon and boron nucleophiles to the 1,3‐diene unit of methylene cyclobutenes is reported. Si─B and B─B reagents serve as silicon and boron pronucleophiles, respectively. Notably, this protocol not only constitutes the unprecedented catalytic asymmetric synthesis of cyclobutanes containing a stereogenic, silicon‐substituted quaternary carbon atom but also provides an efficient access to their boron‐substituted analogs. The transformation proceeds with excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee) and regioisomeric ratios (up to r.r. > 20:1). The substrate scope is broad, and the resulting silicon‐ and boron‐substituted products can be engaged in diverse downstream functional‐group manipulations, underscoring the synthetic utility of this methodology.

title: Fully π‐Conjugated Nonvolatile n‐Type Additives Toward 21% Efficiency in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid additive engineering represents a key strategy to modulate the morphology of organic solar cells via intermolecular interactions (van der Waals forces, hydrogen bonds, and dipole interaction) with photoactive materials. However, these weak interactions lack sufficient capacity to control the crystallization and phase separation of active layer. Here, we developed a conjugated electrostatic coupling strategy to strengthen the intermolecular forces between solid additives and donor/acceptor. The solid additive we designed possesses a fully conjugated structure that can generate strong electrostatic potential interaction, therefore a small amount of solid additive (3 wt%) facilitate ordered crystalline fibril growth of polymer donor and dense molecular packing of acceptor. In addition, the n‐type nature and nonvolatile feature of solid additive promotes the electron transport capacity and stability of the active layer. As a result, the optimal device achieved a state‐of‐the‐art efficiency of 21.02% (certificated to 20.55%), due to the prolonged exciton lifetime, suppressed charge recombination, and enhanced charge collection efficiency. This work establishes a new paradigm for solid additive engineering in organic photovoltaics.

title: Genetic control of active matter
Solvent‐Induced Reversible Phase Transition in Microporous Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks for Molecular‐Sieving Separation of CO 2 and C 2 H 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient separation of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) remains a critical challenge in the chemical industry for C 2 H 2 purification, due to their highly similar molecular sizes and physicochemical property. Here we report a HOF material, denoted HIAM‐105, assembled from a tetracarboxylic acid building block. It undergoes reversible structural transformation upon solvent removal and inclusion. The guest‐free structure (HIAM‐105a) features precisely matched pore dimensions with CO 2 molecules while fully excluding C 2 H 2 , enabling molecular sieving separation of CO 2 /C 2 H 2 . At 298 K and 1 bar, HIAM‐105a achieves a CO 2 adsorption capacity of 44.0 cm 3 g −1 , resulting in a CO 2 /C 2 H 2 adsorption capacity ratio as high as 23.9, which outperforms most previously reported sieving adsorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm that HIAM‐105a can produce C 2 H 2 with ultrahigh purity from CO 2 /C 2 H 2 mixtures, and more importantly, it can be readily regenerated through gas purging at ambient conditions.

title: Programmable Interfacial Evolution in Seawater Iodine Batteries Guided by an Electrochemical Vector‐Coupled Free‐Energy Descriptor
abstract: ABSTRACT Interface, as predominant electrochemical reaction region at the metal anode, has to face challenging issues in harsh seawater environment. Highly reactive soluble halogen intermediates can facilitate the multiple electron transfer process during electrochemical reaction, but the severe shuttle behaviors and cascade corrosion would become more serious in chlorine enriched seawater electrolyte. Conventional solution focused on static interfacial regulation with strong confinement, the lack of dynamical electrochemical response results in irreversible active iodine loss, further accelerate the battery failure. Given that, we proposed a novel theoretical descriptor to qualify electrochemical vector coupled free energy landscape, denoted as 𝒢 ev ( E , Δ G 0 ). By coupling electric filed with free energy, the electrochemically programming interface with dynamic self‐adaptive halogen regulation (AHR) can be described quantitively. Taking an α‐aminoketone‐contained bio‐interface as an example, along with the polarization variation over electrochemical reaction, the interface enables reversible capture to release shift of halogen intermediates, and thus realize reversible modulation of Cl‐coordinated iodine species by leveraging thermodynamic gating mechanism. An emergency power supply system based on seawater‐activated flexible fiber batteries could well operate in underwater portable situation. Our work unveils a novel research perspective on interface regulation strategies, to build an initiative adaptive interface rather than conventional ways.

title: Synergistic Coordination and Crosslinking Strategy for Scalable, Self‐Repairable C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 Separation Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Ethylene/ethane (C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 ) separation is one of the most energy‐intensive processes in the chemical industry, and membrane technology offers a promising low‐energy alternative. However, conventional mixed‐matrix membranes (MMMs) suffer from poor filler dispersion and interfacial defects, especially at high MOF loadings. Here we report a synergistic coordination and crosslinking strategy to fabricate highly compatible, high‐loaded UTSA‐280‐integrated hydrogel MMMs for efficient C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 separation. By exploiting the dual role of calcium ions (Ca 2+ ), which simultaneously coordinate with squaric acid to grow UTSA‐280 and crosslink sodium alginate (SA) chains, we achieve in situ growth of uniformly dispersed UTSA‐280 nanoparticles (mean size 4.32 nm) within a semisolid hydrogel network. The resulting membrane exhibits a high MOF loading of 27.39 wt%, a C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 mixture separation factor of 4.0 at 7 bar, and stable operation for over 1780 h. The hydrogel matrix also confers a remarkable self‐repair capability, fully restoring separation performance after mechanical damage. Moreover, a 200 cm 2 large‐area membrane was readily fabricated, demonstrating a cost‐effective route to scalable ethylene purification.

title: Single Chiroptical Pulse in Non‐Equilibrium Supramolecular Systems via Inter‐Macrocyclic Crosstalk
abstract: ABSTRACT Can an autonomous triphasic temporal pulse emerge in supramolecular architectures without relying on chemical transformations or external chemical fuel? Here, we demonstrate sequential chiroptical sign reversals in a time‐dependent, aperiodic circular dichroism waveform excursion governed purely by non‐covalent binding kinetics in a dual‐receptor network of pillar[5]arene and prism[5]arene. Challenging an established chiral equilibrium with an antipodal alanine derivative induces an out‐of‐equilibrium optical pulse that inverts the chiroptical sign before settling into a persistent state. This transient behavior originates from the synergy between mismatched macrocyclic binding/unbinding rates and ultra‐fast racemization of planar chirality during competitive ligand exchange, as verified by time‐resolved spectroscopy and kinetic modeling. Tailoring receptor substituents and component ratios enables straightforward regulation over both duration and amplitude of the transient response. By establishing indirect intermolecular signal relays through shared effectors, this work provides a transformative blueprint for engineering dissipative systems‐level dynamics in non‐reactive, life‐like materials.

title: Thorium and Uranium Cyaphido and Pnictaethynolato Complexes
abstract: ABSTRACT The synthesis of a homologous series of tris(hexamethyldisilazide) thorium(IV) and uranium(IV) complexes bearing phosphaethynolate (OCP), arsaethynolate (OCAs), and cyaphide (CP) ligands is reported. These species were characterized by multi‐element NMR spectroscopy ( 1 H, 13 C{ 1 H} and 31 P), IR spectroscopy and single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction. A structural comparison of the compounds reveals interesting geometric variations, with the pnictaethynolate complexes favoring strictly trigonal pyramidal geometries, whereas the cyaphide compounds display moderately more tetrahedral coordination environments, approaching those of the chlorido precursors [An{N(SiMe 3 ) 2 } 3 Cl] (An = U, Th). We attribute these subtle structural differences to the covalency of the metal–ligand interactions. This hypothesis was probed using density functional theory, which showed that the computed gas‐phase structures of the compounds do indeed match those determined experimentally. Electronically speaking, the An–OCE bonds were found to be almost purely ionic (with polarization to the pseudo‐halide oxygen atoms ranging from 95%–100%). In these complexes, the highly Lewis acidic character of the metals pulls them into the plane defined by the amide ligands to maximize metal–hexamethyldisilazide interactions. By contrast, the An–CP bonds have greater covalent character than those observed for the pnictaethynolate complexes, with a lesser degree of polarization and higher Wiberg bond indices.

title: Engineered Pore Bisection by a Cymbal‐Shaped Cycloaliphatic Pillar in a Zn‐Triazolate Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) for Selective CO 2 Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Physisorbents combining ultramicroporosity, high CO 2 affinity, and humidity tolerance remain a challenge in carbon‐capture materials. MOFs based on flexible Zn‐triazolate layers have emerged as a promising platform; however, balancing pore size, confinement, and regeneration remains nontrivial. Here we introduce a new pillared‐layer MOF, ZnTzBCP, constructed from Zn 2 + cations, 1,2,4‐triazolate (Tz) linkers, and the 3‐dimensional cycloaliphatic bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane‐1,3‐dicarboxylate (BCP) linker. Liquid‐assisted mechanochemical grinding affords a crystalline material in which the rigid BCP pillars with a cymbal‐shaped core bisect the pore space into symmetric twin ultramicropores with dimensions commensurate with the CO 2 kinetic diameter. Combined PXRD/PW‐DFT/Rietveld analysis integrated with gas sorption, calorimetry, and CO 2 ‐loaded structural refinement reveals reversible, guest‐responsive flexibility of the Zn‐Tz layers through anisotropic swelling of the MOF with CO 2 molecules generating multiple cooperative C─H···O interactions with both ligands and yielding high adsorption enthalpies of 41 kJ/mol. These properties are retained in a PVDF composite, which demonstrates stable, cyclic CO 2 capture under humid breakthrough conditions with minimal thermal regeneration (333 K) and outstanding selectivity for CO 2 over nitrogen of 226. These findings position the linkers with a cymbal‐shaped core as powerful pore‐controlling elements for the design of ultramicroporous MOFs capable of selective CO 2 capture under operative conditions.

title: Oxygen Facilitated Aqueous Photomediated‐RAFT Polymerization: Just Add Salt
abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, we report the first example of a novel oxygen‐facilitated photoinitiation system by employing a combination of riboflavin 5’‐monophosphate sodium salt (Vitamin B2) and disodium hydrogen phosphate (Na 2 HPO 4 ) for conducting reversible addition–fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization. Under blue LED irradiation (λ = 451 nm) and an oxygen atmosphere, the bioactive form of riboflavin, flavin mononucleotide, in the presence of first Na 2 HPO 4 and then extended to other salts, was able to initiate the controlled RAFT polymerization of N,N ‐dimethylacrylamide. The resulting polymer was found to also possess excellent chain fidelity after chain extension via characterization by gel permeation chromatography. These photopolymerizations were found to only proceed to high conversion in the presence of both oxygen and salt. Exploiting the oxygen‐facilitated and aqueous nature of our system, we could achieve microliter‐scale polymerization in mammalian cell culture medium in the presence of live cells.

title: Diversified Synthesis of Nonclassical C ‐Glycosides Through Cooperative N ‑Heterocyclic Carbene and Photoredox Catalytic Acylation
abstract: ABSTRACT C ‐Glycosides have attracted sustained interest because of their exceptional metabolic stability and diverse biological activities; nevertheless, they remain far less explored than their O ‐ and N ‐glycoside counterparts. In particular, the diversified synthesis of nonclassical C ‐glycosides constitutes an even more formidable challenge in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report an N ‐heterocyclic carbene (NHC)/photoredox dual‐catalytic strategy that installs proximal and remote acyl groups at non‐anomeric positions of saccharides, delivering structurally unique nonclassical C ‐glycosides. The installed acyl groups function as versatile synthetic linchpins that can be readily converted into various aglycone functionalities, including alkenyl, hydroxyalkyl, and allyl groups. This protocol facilitates the diversity‐oriented synthesis of several medicinally interesting C ‐glycosides, including indole‐ and quinoline‐containing C ‐glycosides, as well as ribosyl Z‐/E‐ tamoxifen analogues. Preliminary mechanistic studies, including control experiments and photochemical investigations, support a radical catalytic manifold. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further rationalize the high stereoselectivity observed in the glycosylation steps of the two‐component and three‐component reactions, respectively.

title: An Adsorption‐Driven Solvophobic Interface for Stable Lithium‐Rich Manganese‐Based Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based (LRMO) oxides represent the premier cathode candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries due to high specific capacity exceeding 300 mAh g −1 . However, the practical deployment of LRMO cathodes under high voltages (>4.8 V) is severely hindered by severe electrolyte oxidation and transition‐metal (TM) dissolution. Herein, perfluorobutanesulfonyl fluoride (NfF) is introduced as a multifunctional additive to construct a robust solvophobic interphase on LRMO cathodes. The ‐SO 2 F group preferentially anchors to exposed TM sites, suppressing metal dissolution, while the perfluorinated chain excludes free solvent molecules from the cathode surface and mitigates oxidative electrolyte decomposition. The resulting inorganic‐rich (LiF/Li x SO y ) engineered interface mitigates the irreversible layered‐to‐spinel phase transition and inhibits TM crosstalk to the lithium metal anode, ensuring exceptional structural integrity and rapid ionic transport kinetics. Consequently, Li||LRMO coin cells sustain over 1000 cycles at 3 C. The Li||LRMO full cells based on a 40 µm lithium anode and cathode loading of 8 mg cm −2 retain 173 mAh g −1 after 110 cycles. Moreover, the 1.2 Ah Li||LRMO pouch cells achieve 88% capacity retention after 50 cycles at 4.8 V. This work demonstrates solvophobic interphase engineering as an effective strategy for stabilizing high‐voltage cathodes through coordinated regulation of interfacial chemistry and electrolyte accessibility.

title: Polyanion‐Modulated Vanadium‐Doped Ammonium Iron Phosphate Framework from Spent LiFePO 4 for Lattice Oxygen‐Participated Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Promoting the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) offers an effective route to improving the efficiency of water electrolysis. However, achieving efficient LOM operation in structurally stable catalysts remains challenging. To address this challenge, we report a microwave‐assisted upcycling strategy using spent LiFePO 4 as a lithium‐deficient precursor. The cycling‐induced lithium deficiency facilitates structural reorganization into a polyanion‐modulated vanadium‐doped ammonium iron phosphate hydroxide hydrate (S‐VAFP) without residual Li‐containing impurities. The resulting S‐VAFP features a three‐dimensional polyanionic framework composed of FeO 6 octahedra vertex‐linked with PO 4 tetrahedra, forming one‐dimensional channels that promote electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This architecture tunes Fe─O covalency, weakens Fe─(O─P) linkages, and drives in situ reconstruction into a catalytically active amorphous phase, thereby facilitating lattice oxygen participation. Chemical probe experiments and 18 O isotope‐labeling DEMS further verify the AEM–LOM coupled OER pathway. Benefiting from this structure‐guided LOM activation, S‐VAFP delivers an overpotential of 250 mV at 100 mA cm −2 with a Tafel slope of 47.2 mV dec ‒1 . An assembled anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) cell achieves 1.72 V at 1 A cm −2 with stability exceeding 1000 h. Overall, this work establishes polyanion‐mediated electronic modulation as an effective strategy for designing stable iron phosphate electrocatalysts with enhanced lattice oxygen participation.

title: Operando Pressure Monitoring, EIS, and X‐Ray Imaging of Solid‐State Sodium‐Sulfur Batteries — Insights into Chemo‐Mechanical Degradation Mechanisms
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we introduce a multi‐modal operando platform that combines cell stack pressure monitoring, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and x‐ray imaging to unravel the chemo‐mechanical aging processes in sulfide‐based solid‐state sodium‐sulfur (ssNa||S) cells. Despite their promising theoretical capacity and resource abundance, the mechanisms that limit the full performance of ssNa||S batteries are still poorly understood. To address this issue, we employ a new multi‐modal operando setup optimized for solid‐state cells. By comparing cells with different electrolytes, Na 3 PS 4 (NPS), a multiphase electrolyte Na 2 S‐P 2 S 5 ‐NaCl (NPS‐Cl), and Na 3 SbS 4 (NSbS), operando over the course of 50 cycles, we monitor slowly evolving aging effects that are found to be correlated with the electrolyte composition. For NPS, the combination of low interfacial stability against sodium and reduced ionic conductivity causes the electrochemical activity to be concentrated in localized regions, leading to sodium plating‐like behavior as the dominant degradation mechanism. In contrast, the chloride‐containing NPS‐Cl enhances the interfacial stability and mitigates dendrite formation. These findings provide valuable insights for the materials development of sulfide‐based electrolytes for ssNa||S cells and demonstrate the capability of combined operando diagnostics to resolve complex chemo‐mechanical phenomena that influence solid‐state battery performance.

title: Directed Perovskite‐to‐Fullerene Electron Shuttle for 27.2% Inverted Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Although C 60 is almost exclusively used in the electron transport layers of high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), its weak affinity and unfavorable energy level alignment with perovskite lead to weak contact and mismatch in the conduction band level at the perovskite/C 60 interface, thereby limiting further improvement of device efficiency as well as compromising device long‐term operational stability. We synthesized an n ‐type Pyridinium molecule, 2,7‐di(pyridin‐4‐yl)benzo[lmn][3,8]phenanthroline‐1,3,6,8(2H,7H)‐tetraone dihydroiodide (PPTHI), and used it as the interfacial electron‐selective contact in inverted PSCs. The pyridinium iodide head unit in the PPTHI anchored to the halide vacancies and coordinated with the exposed lead. Moreover, the π‐conjugated core renders desirable electron‐transport capability, and the n ‐type interfacial modulator can also serve as an electron shuttle between perovskite and the C 60 electron transport layer. The improved electron extraction, optimized energetic, and passivated top surface translated to reduced V OC losses, leading to a certified stabilized power output efficiency of 26.54% and a champion device with an efficiency of 27.2% and a fill factor of 87.17%. Moreover, inverted PSCs incorporating the electron shuttle maintained over 80% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking.

title: Synergistic Interfacial and Subsurface Stabilization of O3‐Type Na‐Ni‐Fe‐Mn‐O Cathodes through Integrated Zr Modification
abstract: ABSTRACT Surface degradation, electrolyte‐derived hydrogen fluoride (HF) attack, and anisotropic phase evolution limit the stability of O3‐type sodium cathodes. An integrated Zr‐based surface/subsurface strategy is developed for Na[Ni 0.3 Fe 0.3 Mn 0.4 ]O 2 (NFM). Treatment at 800°C converts residual Na 2 CO 3 /NaOH into a Na 2 ZrO 3 ‐rich surface nanolayer, accompanied by limited near‐surface Zr incorporation. In hard‐carbon full cells, NFM‐Zr‐800 delivers ∼150 mAh g −1 with ∼87% initial Coulombic efficiency and retains 61.8% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C, compared with 26.4% for bare NFM. Operando X‐ray diffraction shows reduced anisotropic lattice variation during the P3‐to‐OP2 transition. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, Mössbauer spectroscopy, and hybrid‐functional calculations indicate Ni/Fe‐dominated cationic redox, nearly tetravalent Mn, and no major lattice‐oxygen redox contribution. Coulomb–Buckingham calculations suggest that Zr incorporation at Mn sites is energetically favored near the surface within the adopted model. The Na 2 ZrO 3 ‐rich layer mitigates HF‐related interfacial degradation and promotes a Zr–F‐containing protective interface, suppressing transition‐metal dissolution, cathode–electrolyte interphase thickening, particle cracking, and surface reconstruction. These coupled interfacial and structural effects improve the long‐term stability of O3‐type NFM cathodes.

title: Direct Solar Storage and On‐Demand Power via Threshold‐Matched Silicon Photovoltaics and Dual‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct integration of photovoltaics with batteries is attractive for energy‐autonomous mobile platforms, but mismatched photovoltaic output and battery charging requirements, limited high‐rate capability, and low‐temperature degradation can necessitate intermediate power electronics and restrict burst‐power delivery. Here, a threshold‐matched silicon photovoltaic–dual‐ion battery (PV–DIB) architecture is demonstrated by directly coupling a voltage‐ and current‐tailored crystalline‐silicon photovoltaic module with a high‐voltage dual‐ion battery pouch cell. Under one‐sun illumination, the photovoltaic module supplies ≈72 mA at the battery charging threshold, enabling direct charging without intermediate power‐conversion hardware. This matching establishes two complementary operating regimes: solar‐sustained operation when photovoltaic current meets the load demand and on‐demand battery assistance when the load exceeds the photovoltaic input. The integrated system delivers a maximum power density of 11,430 W kg −1 at 40.83 mA cm −2 , maintains stable operation under drone‐relevant dynamic load profiles, and the DIB retains 5,088 W kg −1 at −10°C. Indoor and outdoor flight demonstrations validate direct solar energy storage and burst‐power delivery, establishing threshold matching as a practical design strategy for power‐electronics‐minimized, energy‐autonomous mobile systems.

title: Broadband Aeolian Vibration Harvesting and Electrical‐Damping‐Induced Suppression via Triboelectric‐Electromagnetic Coupling Mechanism
abstract: ABSTRACT Overhead transmission lines have long faced dual threats: a scarcity of power for sensor nodes and fatigue caused by aeolian vibrations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a synergistic strategy that integrates energy harvesting with vibration suppression, transforming vibration energy dissipation into a coupled process of electrical energy conversion and vibration suppression. Based on this strategy, a triboelectric‐electromagnetic coupling device (TECD) is developed. By leveraging the complementary frequency‐domain characteristics of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) and electromagnetic generators (EMGs), as well as the electrical damping generated during the energy conversion process, the device achieves deep synergy between wideband energy harvesting and vibration suppression. Experimental results demonstrate that the TECD can stably charge a 47 µF capacitor to a 5.2 V supply threshold at any frequency within the 5–50 Hz range, reaching a peak output power of up to 287.28 mW. Simultaneously, the associated electrical damping effectively suppresses vibrations, reducing the vibration acceleration of the primary structure by 86% under 30 Hz excitation. Built upon this device, an integrated harvesting‐suppression‐sensing system is constructed, paving a new path for self‐powered state monitoring and structural protection of transmission lines.

title: Interface‐to‐Bulk Grain Regulation Enables Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 Solar Cells Exceeding 11% Efficiency
abstract: ABSTRACT Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) represents an emerging thin‐film photovoltaic absorber owing to the excellent stability, tunable bandgap (1.1–1.7 eV), and high light absorption coefficient (> 10 5 cm −1 ). Hydrothermally deposited Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells have broken the 10% efficiency bottleneck, yet as‐prepared Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 films suffer from small grains (typically ∼400 nm) with abundant grain boundaries (GBs) that introduce dense defect states, inducing severe non‐radiative recombination and hindering further efficiency enhancement. Here we develop an interface‐to‐bulk grain regulation strategy to achieve ultra‐large (exceeding 3 µm) columnar grains spanning the entire absorber. This strategy combines buried‐interface Sb pre‐deposition to tailor initial hydrothermal deposition and rear‐interface Se‐mediated two‐step post‐annealing to drive grain coalescence and growth through a sequential infiltration‐reaction‐coalescence mechanism. We also found that this grain engineering also leads to the passivation of bulk deep‐level and interfacial defects, and optimized heterojunction band alignment, which collectively suppresses non‐radiative recombination and in turn delivers an ultralow open‐circuit voltage deficit of 0.483 V. Consequently, the ultra‐large‐grain Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cell delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 11.04%, which is the highest efficiency ever reported for antimony chalcogenide‐based solar cells. This study establishes an integrated strategy for regulating grain growth in Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 films toward efficient devices.

title: A Spin‐Crossover Neutral‐Site Perovskite Ferroelectric
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskites have emerged as a globally researched family of multifunctional materials, benefiting from their rich physical properties. However, despite extensive investigations into their ferroelectric and magnetic properties, the coexistence of ferroelectricity and spin crossover (SCO) within perovskites remains largely unexplored. Herein, by combining perovskites and coordination polymers (CPs), we designed the first perovskite SCO ferroelectric, [Fe(4‐ATA) 3 ]SiF 6 (4‐ATA = 4‐amino‐1,2,4‐triazole), which adopts an uncommon neutral site (4‐ATA). The order‐disorder transition of 4‐ATA ligands induces a 6/ m F6‐type ferroelectric phase transition at 331 K, with a spontaneous polarization of 4.0 µC/cm 2 . Notably, [Fe(4‐ATA) 3 ]SiF 6 exhibits a SCO transition at 253 K within the ferroelectric phase, accompanied by distortion of the FeN 6 octahedron. Moreover, we observed a switchable magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) signal during the SCO transition. Our discovery opens a new avenue for the design of SCO ferroelectrics and sheds light on the further exploration of CP perovskite SCO ferroelectrics.

title: Porous Organic Frameworks for Overall Photosynthesis H 2 O 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐to‐H 2 O 2 conversion represents one of the most promising avenues for sustainable development, while overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via the dual pathways of simultaneous ORR and WOR holds significant scientific value. This review first systematically summarizes the recent advancements of porous organic frameworks (POFs) for overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Starting with a concise overview of the fundamental principles of H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via ORR and WOR, as well as dual‐channel H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, the evaluation protocols and key factors are briefly discussed. Thereafter, the advantages, development, and typical design strategies of POFs for this process are summarized. Subsequently, various smart POFs for dual‐pathway photosynthesis H 2 O 2 are introduced. In the past year alone, diverse molecular design strategies have driven continuous gains across all performance metrics, with records reaching a H 2 O 2 production rate of 17.25 mmol·g −1 h −1 , an accumulated concentration of 82.3 mM, an AQY of 40%, and an SCC efficiency of 4.7%. Last but not least, conclusions, challenges, and long‐term outlooks of this field are revealed with a focus on POFs design, computer‐assist, H 2 O 2 decomposition, and mechanism investigations. This review aims to offer in‐depth insights and guidelines for POFs in efficient overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis.

title: Steric Effect of Branch Grafting Enables Highly Soluble and Stable Phenazines in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Phenazine‐based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one‐step two‐electron redox reaction. However, the highly conjugated structure of phenazine reduces molecular polarity and limits the solubility in electrolytes. Herein, we introduced a branched chain to achieve a highly stable and soluble phenazine derivative for AOFBs. The branched structure can effectively suppress the π – π interaction of the phenazine conjugation system but also inhibit the hydrolysis of the ether bond by steric hindrance, which significantly enhances the structural stability. The AOFB using a 1.0 mol/L electrolyte of 2,2′‐(phenazine‐2,3‐diylbis(oxy))dipropionic acid exhibited a high discharge capacity of 45.5 Ah/L and a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.00017% per cycle, with stable operation for more than 42 days (1200 cycles). Furthermore, a pilot‐scale stack demonstrated excellent cycling stability, with negligible capacity degradation after 400 cycles. The outstanding AOFB performance suggests its promise for large‐scale energy storage applications.

title: Synthetic Control of Oxygen Transport in Ultra‐Low Density Amorphous Thin Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Ion transport is a critical functional property of many energy and electronic materials. In noncrystalline materials, it is believed that ion conductivity depends on density and free volume; however, it is difficult to tune density by more than 1% through melt‐quench synthesis. In this work, we use physical vapor deposition to deposit HfO 2 thin films with over 30% tunability in density. Isotope tracing shows that the oxygen tracer diffusivity of ultra‐low‐density films is about three orders of magnitude higher than that of higher‐density analogs. Molecular dynamics simulations similarly demonstrate this ability to control oxygen transport via density and further show that correlation effects are a plausible contributor to the density‐dependent diffusivities. Our work reveals that the mass density is an important yet routinely unreported parameter controlling oxygen transport in amorphous materials. This principle opens a new design space for the synthesis of thin‐film ion conductors.

title: Gradient‐Engineered Hole‐Selective Contact Layers via Spatially Confined Annealing for Efficient Tin–Lead and All‐Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole‐selective contact layers (HSLs) govern charge extraction and interfacial energetics in perovskite solar cells, yet conventional designs are largely limited to planar architectures with homogeneous electronic properties. Such planar HSLs are insufficient for mixed tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites, where short carrier diffusion lengths require efficient three‐dimensional charge‐collection pathways. Here, a spatially confined molecular‐gradient engineering strategy is introduced to construct energetic‐cascade HSLs within mesoporous frameworks. A screened and optimized phosphonic‐acid self‐assembled monolayer, [2‐(7H‐dibenzo[c,e]carbazol‐7‐yl)ethyl] phosphate, is incorporated into a mesoporous indium tin oxide nanocrystal matrix. Spatially confined annealing drives directional molecular redistribution, generating a controllable bottom‐to‐surface concentration gradient. This gradient establishes continuous energy cascades and graded hole‐transport channels, while simultaneously modulating the crystallization of the overlying Sn–Pb perovskite to suppress nonradiative recombination. Single‐junction Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 24.14%, and monolithic two‐terminal all‐perovskite tandem solar cells reach 29.56% efficiency with substantially improved operational stability. More broadly, this work establishes molecular‐gradient engineering in porous matrices as a versatile strategy for programming charge transport and interfacial chemistry in solution‐processed optoelectronic devices.

title: Spontaneous Emulsification of Long‐Chain Alkanes to Form Oil‐in‐Water Nano‐Emulsions
abstract: ABSTRACT Spontaneous emulsification (SE) of long‐chain alkanes (LCA) to form oil‐in‐water (O/W) emulsion (SE‐O/W‐LCA) holds significant promise for applications such as oil sands extraction. However, SE‐O/W‐LCA remains a long‐standing challenge due to the extremely low polarity of LCA and high oil‐water interfacial tension. Herein, we present a successful strategy for achieving SE‐O/W‐LCA based on the design of surfactant molecular architecture. Systematic studies on structure–activity relationship correlating the structure of surfactant molecular segments with SE performance lead to an optimized surfactant architecture that achieves an emulsification capacity approximately two orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional surfactants. A general design guideline of surfactants is established, requiring both high LCA solubility and large hydrophilic–lipophilic balance (HLB) values for efficient SE. Fundamentally, the integrated SE mechanism, involving reverse‐micelle diffusion, Marangoni‐flow and O/W droplet formation, is elucidated alongside the corresponding thermodynamic basis and kinetic evolution. Finally, the developed strategy is successfully applied to practical oil sands extraction that delivers state‐of‐the‐art oil‐solid separation performance as compared with previously reported methods. The proposed SE‐O/W‐LCA strategy, together with the understanding of surfactant design guidelines and underlying mechanisms, is anticipated to inspire future research on low‐energy emulsification and advance the widespread industrial deployment of SE technology.

title: Understanding Activation Energies of Dark Currents in Shortwave Infrared Organic Photodiodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of near‐infrared (NIR) and shortwave‐infrared (SWIR) organic photodetectors (OPDs) has been fundamentally hindered by high dark current, which is often considered an intrinsic limitation. This stems from the prevailing model where trap‐assisted thermal generation caps the dark current activation energy ( E a ) at half the material's effective bandgap (). Here, we demonstrate that this perceived limit is not fundamental and can be surpassed. By systematically engineering thick‐film devices to suppress trap‐mediated recombination and shunt pathways, we demonstrate a transition to a bulk‐limited, band‐to‐band‐like thermal generation regime. This allows the activation energy to approach the effective bandgap ( E a ≈ ), far above the limit of trap‐assisted generation. Our findings provide a direct design principle for fabricating NIR and SWIR OPDs with substantially lower dark currents.

title: High‐Efficiency Solution‐Processed Sensitized OLEDs With Low Roll‐Off Enabled by Near‐Ultraviolet Emissive Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescent Polysiloxanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving solution‐processed high‐efficiency blue OLEDs with low efficiency roll‐off remains a challenge. In this study, a siloxane‐backbone engineering strategy is proposed to develop near‐ultraviolet emissive thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers that can multifunctionally serve as emitter/host/sensitizer for solution‐processed blue OLEDs. Benefiting from good film‐forming ability, balanced carrier transport and efficient exciton utilization, the non‐doped OLEDs based on the prepared TADF polysiloxane, PSiCzBN 1 mCP 9 , achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) of 8.2% with an electroluminescence peak at 394 nm. Notably, two TADF polysiloxanes are further used as host or sensitizer in hyperfluorescence and phosphor‐assisted TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (pTSF) devices. The solution‐processed blue pTSF device exhibits a high EQE max of 35.7%, placing it among the one of the best‐performing TADF polymeric OLEDs reported to date. This work demonstrates that siloxane‐backbone engineering is an effective design strategy for achieving high‐efficiency solution‐processed blue OLEDs by regulating film morphology and excited‐state energy level, simultaneously.

title: Inactivation of the RB1 and PTPN14 tumor suppressors cooperatively enables the lifespan extension activity of the human papillomavirus E7 oncoprotein
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) E7 proteins bind and inactivate host cellular tumor suppressors and are essential for the immortalization of primary human keratinocytes. E7 proteins from high- and low-risk HPV genotypes bind directly to at least two tumor suppressors, RB1 and PTPN14, and inactivate both. We previously characterized mutations in high-risk HPV E7 proteins that selectively abrogate the ability of E7 to bind either RB1 or PTPN14. Here, we established a genetic complementation system using the E7 mutants defective for binding to RB1 or PTPN14. Neither mutant alone could extend the lifespan of primary keratinocytes. When expressed together, the mutants could, like wild-type high-risk HPV E7, extend keratinocyte lifespan. Both high- and low-risk E7 reduced PTPN14 protein levels and reduced expression of keratinocyte differentiation genes, whereas only high-risk E7 reduced steady-state RB1 levels and induced E2F-dependent genes. Depletion of either RB1 or PTPN14 could cooperate with low-risk HPV6 E7 to extend keratinocyte lifespan. Our findings advance the model that inactivation of at least two tumor suppressors is required for the lifespan extension activity of high-risk HPV E7.

title: Protein spherical nucleic acids enable multivalent display of TLR9 agonists for enhanced cancer immunotherapy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Precise control over nanoparticle composition and molecular architecture remains a fundamental challenge in nanomedicine, limiting systematic exploration of therapeutic design and biological function. Here, we report structurally defined protein spherical nucleic acids (ProSNAs) comprising ferritin nanocages densely functionalized with Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist, immunostimulatory oligonucleotide shell for cancer immunotherapy. ProSNAs are rapidly internalized by immune cells, elicit potent innate immune activation, and exhibit prolonged intratumoral retention with preferential uptake by myeloid cells. These responses promote dendritic cell maturation, polarize macrophages toward an antitumor phenotype, and stimulate robust CD8
                    +
                    T cell–mediated immunity. Across murine melanoma, colon adenocarcinoma, and triple-negative breast cancer models, a single intratumoral administration of ProSNAs induces durable tumor regression, suppresses metastatic progression, and synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade. Taken together, these findings establish ProSNAs as a structurally defined, myeloid-targeting nanomedicine platform for programmable cancer immunotherapy.

title: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama’s anchoveta fishery and its exports
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In 2025 the seasonal upwelling of the Gulf of Panama failed. Net primary production fell by 64% across the Gulf and industrial anchoveta landings dropped to 11% of the average, the lowest since the fishery became fully exploited in 1966. Anchoveta caught per purse-seine set fell to under a third of the normal rate while total catch per set stayed within its normal range. Landed fish carried about half their usual lipid content, and fish oil exports fell by 88% in both volume and value. The effects of one failed season reached international trade within months. Seasonal upwellings like this are common across the tropics yet far less studied than the large eastern boundary systems. The very strong El Niño now under way makes the 2027 season more uncertain.

title: Human retinal capillary network analysis using vascular interconnectivity optical coherence tomography angiography
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The human retina is perfused by capillary plexuses at distinct inner-retinal depths. Interconnections among these plexuses are critical for perfusion, but are difficult to quantify using 2D en face optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Diabetic retinopathy (DR) involves extensive microvascular remodeling, however the topological changes, especially at the interplexus level, are challenging to assess in vivo. We introduce Network Analysis using Vascular Interconnectivity (NAVI) OCTA, a framework that reconstructs the 3D retinal capillary network across the superficial vascular (SVP), intermediate capillary (ICP), and deep capillary (DCP) plexuses. The reconstructed macula-wide vasculature contains more than 10,000 vessel segments, and can be quantitatively analyzed using network representation. This method reveals a divergent alteration in interplexus connectivity in early DR: superficial-to-intermediate connections decrease, while intermediate-to-deep connections increase. This finding is consistent with previous histological studies, but is quantitatively measured in vivo in the human retina, opening the possibility for longitudinal studies of capillary remodeling. In addition to size-based metrics (e.g., vessel length or area), NAVI can quantify recurrent small-scale connectivity patterns (motifs). Finally, joint connectivity-hemodynamics analysis is demonstrated in eyes with DR, where capillary topology and flow speed can be quantified using a single OCTA acquisition. NAVI OCTA is a scalable, computational framework that supports analysis of retinal vasculature as a network and provides an in vivo approach to study capillary remodeling in early DR.

title: Senescence markers diverge in space, timing, and phenotypic relevance during skin aging in mice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The cell theory of aging posits that senescent cells accumulate with age, altering their environment and causing functional organ decline. The dynamics of their accumulation during normal aging and the extent to which it contributes to age-associated damage and disease remain unclear. Using the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, which tracks two strains in both sexes, we identified skin health as a strong predictor of frailty. Quantification of three canonical senescence-associated markers (p16, p21, and γH2AX) in the skin of 320 animals showed variable effects of age on marker abundance: p16 increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform changes. Associations between marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous and varied by marker, sex, and strain. These findings underscore a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes, challenging the view that senescent cell accumulation uniformly drives organ decline.

title: A chromatin biology assessment of AlphaFold3
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular structure prediction tools such as AlphaFold have achieved remarkable success in predicting structures of single proteins and multiprotein complexes. AlphaFold3 now incorporates the capability to model complexes containing nucleic acids and chemically modified side chains. Investigators can now predict structures of proteins bound to chromatin, where interactions with nucleosomal DNA and histone posttranslational modifications (PTMs) converge to control genome function. To evaluate its robustness in modeling chromatin complexes, we benchmarked AlphaFold3 on 115 structures containing nucleosomes whose coordinates were released by the Protein Data Bank after the training set cutoff date. We find that AlphaFold3 excels at predicting interactions with the histone octamer core and with PTMs. By contrast, AlphaFold3 struggles to predict structures of chromatin factors that primarily engage nucleosomal DNA, notably transcription factors and chromatin remodelers. We also show that AlphaFold3 can faithfully recapitulate known PTM recognition patterns, matching experimentally determined specificity profiles. This assessment of the capabilities and limitations of AlphaFold3 in chromatin structural biology provides a roadmap for its effective application to studies of chromatin regulation and PTM readout, while identifying key areas for future refinement of algorithms for predicting interactions between proteins and nucleic acids.

title: Promises and pitfalls of community moderation on social media
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Social media platforms have traditionally relied on internal moderation teams and partnerships with independent fact-checking organizations to identify and flag problematic content. Recently, however, platforms including X (formerly Twitter) and Meta have shifted toward community-driven content moderation by launching their own versions of crowd-sourced fact-checking—Community Notes. If effectively scaled and governed, such crowd-checking initiatives have the potential to combat misinformation as successfully as community-driven efforts once did with spam. However, moderating misinformation is inherently more complex: perceptions of truth are often shaped by personal biases, political leanings, and cultural contexts, complicating consensus on what constitutes misleading content. This suggests that community efforts, while valuable, cannot replace the indispensable role of professional fact-checkers. Here we explore the emerging role of community-driven moderation, critically evaluate both the promises and the challenges of Community Notes at scale, and identify how collaborative and technical innovations can integrate the two distinct approaches.

title: Rethinking broad diet breadth as a sign of scarcity: A 50,000-y record of subsistence from northwestern Australia
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The prey choice model, widely applied in archaeological reconstructions of Pleistocene diet, predicts that people will initially focus on a narrow suite of high-ranked prey before broadening their diet to include lower-ranked species as necessitated by subsistence needs. However, evidence from arid and semiarid northern Australia challenges this assumption. Archaeological faunal records demonstrate that a broad diet was established early and persisted through the Holocene. We argue that these diverse diets do not indicate resource scarcity, but rather represent an ideal strategy for exploiting abundant, low-risk hidden, or cryptic prey, as well as high-risk, conspicuous prey within an environment characterized by unpredictable rainfall. This pattern also necessitates reconceptualizing traditional notions of prey rank and dietary breadth. Rather than adhering to static prey rankings, northern Australian peoples skillfully adapted their hunting strategies in response to fluctuating nutritional content and pursuit costs of different species. The most successful subsistence strategy in this region was therefore one of high responsiveness and flexibility, manifesting as a consistently broad diet. This case study suggests that the relationship between human dietary breadth and resource abundance is more nuanced in situations of abundant, cryptic prey.

title: Wnts are endothelial cell–derived PKD1/PKD2-dependent autocrine/paracrine vasodilators
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Wingless/Int-1 (Wnts) are secreted glycoproteins and canonical Frizzled receptor ligands. Recent evidence indicates that some Wnts can also bind to polycystin 1 (PKD1), a large transmembrane protein which can couple to polycystin 2 (PKD2) to form a nonselective cation channel. The functional significance of PKD1, PKD2, and Wnt-mediated PKD1 signaling in native cell types is poorly understood. Here, we tested the hypothesis that Wnts regulate arterial contractility, investigated the signaling mechanisms and cell types involved, and examined the cellular source of vasoactive Wnts. Our data show that Wnt9b and Wnt5a are endothelial cell (EC)-dependent vasodilators. Wnt9b stimulates vasodilation via EC PKD1/PKD2, whereas Wnt5a acts via both EC PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors. Wnts stimulate endothelial nitric oxide synthase and small conductance Ca
                    2+
                    -activated K
                    +
                    channels in ECs to produce vasodilation. Wnt9b and Wnt5a are present in plasma and intravenous infusion of Wnt9b stimulates an EC PKD1-dependent reduction in systemic blood pressure. Intravascular flow activates angiotensin II type 1 receptors which, through G
                    q/11
                    and Porcupine signaling, stimulate ECs to secrete Wnt9b and Wnt5a. Wnts which are secreted by ECs in response to flow activate PKD1/PKD2 on ECs and this mechanism contributes to the flow-mediated vasodilation. In summary, we show that Wnts are autocrine/paracrine vasodilator proteins. Intravascular flow stimulates ECs to secrete Wnts, which then act via PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors on ECs to induce vasodilation.

title: Tumor cell–intrinsic E47 functions as a critical suppressor in antitumor immunity via the FBXL2–PD-L1 axis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The transcription factor E47, encoded by the
                    TCF3
                    gene, is essential for B and T cell lineage commitment and development. However, whether tumor cell–intrinsic E47 contributes to tumor immunosurveillance remains unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that E47 functions as a critical suppressor of antitumor immunity. Clinical analyses reveal that increased intratumoral
                    TCF3
                    expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Silencing of E47 in tumor cells markedly inhibits tumor growth, increases infiltration of cytotoxic CD8
                    +
                    T cells, and decreases PD-L1 expression. Mechanistically, E47 transcriptionally represses
                    FBXL2
                    , which encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes PD-L1 polyubiquitination at K270 and proteasomal degradation. Restoration of FBXL2 effectively reverses E47-induced PD-L1 upregulation and tumor growth. Strikingly, Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug nebivolol, an activator of FBXL2, significantly enhances antitumor immunity and improves the efficacy of CTLA-4 blockade therapy in syngeneic tumor mouse models. Together, this study uncovers the E47–FBXL2 axis as a critical pathway governing PD-L1 stability and antitumor immunity, highlighting its therapeutic potential for improving the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: NSP1–SAMD9L interactions govern murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Rotavirus replication, pathogenesis, and transmission are host-range restricted, yet the viral and host determinants remain poorly defined. Rotavirus nonstructural protein 1 (NSP1) is a multifunctional innate immune antagonist dispensable for replication in permissive cells. Here, using reverse genetics, neonatal mice, intestinal organoids, and comparative proteomics, we identify mouse SAMD9L as a critical host restriction factor selectively antagonized by murine rotavirus-encoded NSP1. An NSP1-deletion murine-like rotavirus produced progeny efficiently in cell lines but was highly attenuated in neonatal mice with no productive intestinal replication, fecal shedding, and diarrhea. Recombinant monoreassortant viruses carrying NSP1 genes from rhesus, bovine, or human rotavirus strains did not support murine intestinal infection, even in
                    
                      Stat1
                      −/−
                    
                    pups, indicating an additional restriction mechanism beyond STAT1-dependent antiviral signaling. Comparative proteomics identified mouse SAMD9L as a specific interactor of murine NSP1, and NSP1 promoted SAMD9L degradation through a neddylation- and proteasome-dependent pathway. AlphaFold3 guided mutagenesis identified NSP1 residues S364/E366 and SAMD9L residues R455/L462 as functionally important for the NSP1–SAMD9L interaction. Mutations on either side disrupted NSP1–SAMD9L association and prevented SAMD9L degradation. Replication of murine rotaviruses carrying S364A or E366A mutations was undetectable in wild-type mice and was restored in
                    
                      Samd9l
                      −/−
                    
                    mice. Combined deletion of
                    Samd9l
                    and
                    Stat1
                    permitted replication of otherwise attenuated viruses carrying mismatched NSP1s and enabled fecal IgA seroconversion after a single oral inoculation of Rotarix. These findings identify SAMD9L as a physiologically relevant intestinal restriction factor in mice and show that murine NSP1 antagonism of mouse SAMD9L contributes to murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.

title: Unsupervised Bayesian neural networks enable inference of complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Birth–death models quantify macroevolutionary and epidemiological processes, including speciation, extinction, and transmission, based on phylogenetic trees. Extensions of these models incorporate external covariates as predictors of these parameters, for instance linking traits or environmental variables with changes in these rates. However, the dependencies between predictors and model parameters are typically restricted to linear, additive effects and may thus fail to capture complex, nonlinear relationships underlying evolutionary dynamics. To address this limitation, we propose a framework that leverages unsupervised Bayesian neural networks to flexibly model functional relationships between these parameters and a broad set of predictors, including categorical traits, quantitative variables, and time series data. Based on these covariates, the network weights and thus the resulting birth–death dynamics are estimated jointly with the phylogenetic tree, obtained directly from sequence alignment data. Extensive simulations show that this approach accurately recovers predictor–parameter relationships, mitigates overfitting, and remains robust across both macroevolutionary and epidemiological contexts. Using explainable AI, we further show that our framework reliably identifies the most influential predictors and yields interpretable descriptions of their impact on the inferred rates. Finally, we apply our method in two empirical analyses: linking SARS-CoV-2 migration dynamics with travel data during its early spread in Europe, and inferring trait- and time-dependent speciation and extinction rates in the diversification of platyrrhines. Our framework substantially expands the capabilities of birth–death models, providing a powerful and flexible approach to infer complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes.

title: Gammaherpesvirus infection drives genotype-dependent virus-specific T cell responses in the CNS prior to autoimmune neuroinflammation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Infection with the gammaherpesvirus Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) is the strongest environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS). This risk is driven by poor immune control of viral replication, which is genetically determined. Clonally expanded CD8 T cells are abundant in MS lesions, and some recognize EBV antigens. We previously demonstrated that host genetic variation regulates immune control of the homologous B cell–tropic murine gammaherpesvirus, MHV-68. Here, we investigated how gammaherpesvirus infection and host genotype shape central nervous system (CNS) T cell responses, before and after induction of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). Chronic infection alone was sufficient to promote a marked accumulation of CX3CR1+KLRG1+ effector CD8 T cells and CX3CR1+KLRG1+ cytotoxic-like T helper cells in the CNS of MHV-68-susceptible C57BL/6 mice. T cells localized to brain border regions and throughout the CNS parenchyma. MHC tetramer analysis demonstrated that CNS-infiltrating T cells were specific for viral antigens, and viral DNA was detectable in CNS-infiltrating leukocytes during early and chronic infection. EAE further amplified cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS of MHV-68-infected C57BL/6 mice. However, CNS T cell infiltration was highly attenuated in genetically divergent wild-derived PWD/PhJ mice, which control MHV-68 more effectively, but not in MHV-68-susceptible 129S1/SvImJ mice. Surprisingly, chronic MHV-68 infection modestly delayed EAE onset in C57BL/6 mice, an effect reversed by B cell depletion. Together with emerging human studies, our results suggest that host genetic variation contributes to poor control of EBV in MS, promoting virus-specific cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS and immune reprogramming both before and during autoimmune neuroinflammation.

title: Phase coding supports neuronal replication and enables combinatorial problem solving
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Darwinian neurodynamics posits that the brain searches large solution spaces through iterated cycles of variation and selection on competing neural representations. Testing this hypothesis requires a biologically plausible neural replicator: a mechanism that copies spatiotemporal signals faithfully enough to cumulatively improve good solutions, yet loosely enough to allow exploration. We show that phase-coded spike patterns constitute such a replicator. Spike timing referenced to a local field oscillation is compressed into a transferable spike train and reconstructed by coincidence with the receiver’s own field, without synaptic plasticity or a shared code key. As replication noise rises, the system crosses two thresholds. Below the first, faithful copying sustains patterns as dynamic memory. Between the two thresholds, pattern populations evolve. On two hard combinatorial benchmarks, the traveling salesman problem and NK fitness landscapes, neural replication remains competitive with standard search methods at a matched evaluation budget. Beyond the second, an Eigen-like error threshold, inherited information collapses. The network architecture tunes the exploration-exploitation balance: high-degree lattices, where local competition is stronger, exploit smooth landscapes, while low-degree lattices, where weaker competition preserves diversity, search more broadly on rugged landscapes. The framework predicts phase-locked information transfer and phylogenetic structure in replay, as well as a selective loss of combinatorial problem solving beyond the error threshold. These results indicate that a single neurobiological substrate can support memory, variation, and selection, and point to evolutionary dynamics as a candidate computational principle for cognition.

title: Topological validation of generated scientific images
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Synthetic data have become an indispensable tool for validation, standards development, and product design across a broad range of scientific and engineering disciplines. One of the earliest examples arose in energy systems, where security and confidentiality constraints motivated the development of synthetic power grids and, in turn, novel topological and geometric approaches for evaluating their fidelity. Today, synthetic scientific imagery has emerged as a new critical tool in a variety of applications, ranging from autonomous driving, robotics, and Internet-of-Things technologies to in silico trials, digital twins, and remote sensing of environment. Yet the rigorous assessment of such synthetic images and quantification of their associated uncertainties remains a fundamental challenge. Building on the recent advances in the topological and geometric validation of synthetic power grids, we develop a systematic framework for comparing image data through the persistence of their multiscale shape patterns using the statistical formalism of survival analysis. While the tools of persistent homology and statistical survival analysis are both mature methodologies, they have so far developed largely in isolation. Unlike more traditional comparison methods such as pixel-level similarity or distributional summaries that often fail to capture the complex, multiscale structural characteristics of modern scientific imagery, our approach shows the capability to systematically assess the mismatch between different images at all scales simultaneously, while characterizing the associated uncertainty. The resulting synergistic methodology establishes a broadly applicable statistical topological framework for validating synthetic scientific imagery and, more generally, complex synthetic data products.

title: Conditions for runaway ruptures during reservoir operations: Magnitude–frequency distribution implications and application to Groningen
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We present a theoretical analysis of an induced seismic rupture propagating from a gas reservoir into the underburden. We use linear elastic fracture mechanics to determine the conditions for self-arrested or runaway ruptures. We derive a phase diagram in which the model parameters (the reservoir thickness, the reservoir pressure depletion, background stress, and fracture energy) are combined into two dimensionless parameters. We apply the analysis to the seismicity induced by gas extraction from the Groningen gas field, where earthquakes have remained confined to the close vicinity of the reservoir. We invert the observations for the model parameters. They indicate subcritical initial stress on the underburden faults, meaning that runaway ruptures are possible in principle, but the conditions required for such events to have happened were most likely not met in reality. The model reproduces the spatial and temporal patterns of observed maximum earthquake magnitudes, and the significant deficit of
                    M
                    > 3.0 events compared to the expectation from the Gutenberg–Richter relationship. This tapering implies that the expected maximum magnitude is nearly insensitive to the total number of induced earthquakes and strongly controlled by the reservoir thickness and pressure depletion. Because the forecast is probabilistic and accounts for uncertainties in the model parameters, it does not exclude runaway ruptures; but such events are found to be unlikely. The model offers an operational framework to forecast earthquake magnitudes by constraining the physical model with measurable parameters.

title: Reducing belief in conspiracy theories as they unfold using large language models
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The emergence of conspiracy theories in the wake of major events is a significant societal challenge. Here, we test whether conversational dialogues with a large language model (LLM) can reduce belief in immediately unfolding conspiracies. In experiments conducted in the days following the July 2024 assassination attempt on Donald Trump and the September 2025 assassination of Charlie Kirk, US adults (Experiment 1: N = 472; Experiment 2: N = 1,042) holding conspiratorial views about the crisis event engaged in a multiturn conversation with an LLM prompted to reduce their conspiracy belief. Compared to control participants who either discussed an irrelevant topic with an LLM or viewed a static fact sheet, participants in the LLM treatment showed significantly reduced conspiracy beliefs in both experiments. We also found suggestive evidence of downstream effects of the LLM treatment, observing reduced belief in some—but not all—analyses of different conspiratorial beliefs 1 to 2 mo later. These results shed light on the psychology of emerging conspiracies and highlight the potential for scalable, information-focused LLM interventions to counteract misinformation in the immediate aftermath of high-profile societal events.

title: Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex inhibition has potential for shortening leishmaniasis treatment duration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Leishmaniasis affects approximately 1 million people annually with visceral infections resulting in death if left untreated and the cutaneous disease leading to disfiguring skin lesions. Leishmaniasis is caused by the
                    Leishmania
                    spp. parasites and is difficult to treat as existing drugs are far from optimal. Despite increased efforts to identify better drugs for leishmaniasis, there are few new chemical entities that have entered clinical development, thus highlighting the persistent need for such compounds. Here we describe GNF5885, an orally available and parasite-selective inhibitor of
                    Leishmania
                    cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex. GNF5885 was derived through phenotypic optimization of buparvaquone. GNF5885 exhibits unparalleled efficacy in vivo and can efficiently clear parasites from mice in models of visceral and cutaneous infections. Furthermore, its ability to clear parasites rapidly with short treatment regimens makes it particularly desirable for treating patients residing in regions endemic to leishmaniasis. Cryo-EM structure of the
                    Leishmania
                    cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex with GNF5885 at 2.8 Å resolution revealed that the inhibitor binds in the Qi ubiquinone-binding pocket. Our data provide validation of the
                    Leishmania
                    cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex as a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of leishmaniasis and underscore the possibility of developing a short-course oral treatment for this neglected disease. In addition, the availability of the cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex costructure with GNF5885 opens an opportunity to rationally design new cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex inhibitors suitable for clinical development.

title: Humans show limited ability to distinguish human-authored from AI-generated political content on social media
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: This study employs a set of behavioral experiments to examine how individuals perceive the humanness of social media posts about the 2024 U.S. presidential debate between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump. Posts presented in the experiment were authored either by humans or chatbots, varying the large language model (LLM), the model architecture, the social media platform, and the political personas. Participants judged randomly paired posts to identify which they perceived to be AI-generated. We find that human-authored posts were on average perceived as more human-like than AI outputs generated from five of the six LLMs in this study. However, participants’ ability to detect AI-generated content is limited. They do so only slightly above chance in human–AI pairs, and this ability weakens for newer LLMs, varies by platform, and reflects partisan bias. Only posts generated with Llama 3.3 scored, on average, higher on perceived humanness than human-authored posts. The social media platform also mattered, with participants distinguishing human from AI on most platforms (YouTube, TikTok, Truth Social), but not on X/Twitter. Incivility and negative emotions are associated with high humanness perceptions, and partisan identity also shaped evaluations, with Republican respondents more likely to view ideologically misaligned AI posts as AI-generated.

title: Rural outdoor air pollution exceeds urban levels in the Delhi megacity region
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
India routinely experiences some of the highest concentrations of fine particulate matter (PM
                    2.5
                    ) air pollution in the world. Although India’s population predominantly lives in rural areas and smaller cities, policy efforts to date have emphasized air pollution in India’s large cities. In contrast, there is limited understanding of air pollutant dynamics in India’s rural and less urbanized areas. Here, we established a well-calibrated lower-cost PM
                    2.5
                    sensor network spanning a wide range of urbanicity (population densities: 300 to 30,000 people/km
                    2
                    ) outside and inside of Delhi. The network of 49 sites incorporated a 160 km measurement transect to capture ambient PM
                    2.5
                    trends of the Delhi megacity, as well as stratified measurements in villages, small cities, and Delhi itself. We report on data from 5 mo of operation (July–November 2024) spanning the cleanest and most polluted times of the year. PM
                    2.5
                    concentrations at rural sites consistently exceeded those at urban sites by about 20% during every month of our study. Analysis of diurnal PM
                    2.5
                    cycles showed sharp morning (approximately 06:00–10:00 LT) and evening (approximately 16:00–20:00 LT) concentration peaks at rural sites that were absent at urban sites. We attribute these events to widespread use of solid fuels for cooking, heating, and small-scale industry in suburban and rural settings. These striking enhancements in rural air pollution are missed by satellite remote sensing data, and our findings run contrary to the general societal perception that Indian cities are pollution hotspots relative to rural areas.

title: Structural and biochemical impact of clinically relevant constitutively active parathyroid hormone receptor 1 mutations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Parathyroid hormone receptor 1 (PTH1R) constitutively active mutants, including H223
                    2.50
                    R and T410
                    6.42
                    P, are responsible for Jansen’s metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, a form of short-limbed dwarfism. Here, we expand pharmacological understanding and present cryoelectron microscopy structures of the constitutively active PTH1R mutants, H223
                    2.50
                    K, H223
                    2.50
                    R, and T410
                    6.42
                    P, in complex with Gs protein and PTH(1–34), and H223
                    2.50
                    R and T410
                    6.42
                    P in the ligand free Gs complexed form. These reveal modifications in polar networks that allow for constitutive G protein coupling and subsequent signaling. In the absence of a peptide bound to the extracellular side of the PTH1R, TM6 adopts a distinct conformation relative to the PTH(1–34) bound wild-type PTH1R coupled with Gs. Combined with molecular dynamics analysis of inactive and Gs bound receptors, this work reveals distinct mechanisms that lead to differing receptor activation states and consequently promote distinct constitutive activity and agonist-mediated pharmacological profiles.

title: A decavalent Group B streptococcal biosynthetic conjugate vaccine provides functional immunity to all known serotypes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Globally, 394,000 cases of Group B
                    Streptococcus
                    (GBS) infection occur each year, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Vaccination has emerged as an important strategy to limit GBS infections and disease; however, existing vaccine candidates currently in clinical development do not cover all capsular polysaccharide serotypes. Here, we describe the use of a next generation bioconjugation platform to generate a decavalent GBS vaccine (GBS10V) and characterize its immunological evaluation in animals. Using an evolved PglS bioconjugation platform, capsular polysaccharides from all 10 GBS capsular polysaccharide serotypes were individually expressed and bioconjugated to an optimized
                    Pseudomonas aeruginosa
                    exotoxin A (EPA6) carrier protein engineered with six sequons. Multiple biochemical analyses confirmed the identity of each polysaccharide serotype bioconjugated to EPA6. Moreover, intact mass spectrometry (MS) and MS/MS spectra confirmed the presence of sialic acid in each repeat unit of GBS polysaccharides attached to the carrier, an attribute critical for eliciting an optimal immune response. The GBS10V vaccine was used to immunize outbred CD-1 mice and New Zealand White rabbits with doses of 1, 2, or 5 μg per GBS serotype. Sera analyses demonstrated the GBS10V vaccine induced high serotype-specific immunoglobulin titers to all 10 serotypes. Most importantly, interim and postimmune sera from rabbits demonstrated potent opsonophagocytic killing, with median titers ranging from 646 to 6,145 for all serotypes by day 42. Together, these findings establish GBS10V as a global GBS conjugate vaccine candidate for all patient populations, and thus, justify its further preclinical development.

title: Influence of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The effect of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories is investigated. To this end, we first show the equivalence between noninertial effects and a completely positive, trace-preserving (CPTP) map. In this formulation, the Unruh effect is equivalent to a bosonic amplifier channel. The effect of this map on a generic quantum resource is investigated by studying the role of the CPTP map on the three core ingredients of a resource theory, namely, the free states, the free operations, and the resource quantifiers. We show several general statements can be made about these three components of a resource theory in the presence of noninertial motion.
